Name: GSED3.09.story-Charger Information Visibility

If this information is buried or inaccessible, it creates friction for servicing.

Name: GSED3.08.story-Battery Information Visibility
Author: SpencerSkelly

If the charger already has this information via BMID, the HMI should surface it. Otherwise, technicians must put extra effort into finding this information.

Author: SpencerSkelly

If we modernize visually but preserve the same navigation complexity, we haven't truly improved usability.

Name: GSED3.05.story-Charging Mode Visibility

Name: GSED3.04.story-Operational Metrics Visibility

Name: GSED3.10-Charger Settings Access

Name: GSED1-Overview and Context
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
This project defines the product and market requirements required to modernize the GSE charger display interface and enable High Voltage Power Station (HVPS) integration through targeted updates to the existing Gen 3 control architecture.

Originally, GSE display modernization and HVPS communication were expected to be delivered through the broader �Gen 4 / Platform Comms (PCOM)� initiative, which included a new MK3 + adapter board architecture intended to introduce native communications (cellular, Wi-Fi, Ethernet), expanded processing capability, and a modernized display interface across both GSE and MHE portfolios.

Due to cost constraints and architectural complexity, the PCOM initiative was narrowed and ultimately split. The MHE portfolio proceeded with a dedicated communications-focused redesign. The GSE portfolio is now being addressed independently with a more narrow scope.

Name: GSED1.1-Scope of Work
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
The current GSE scope is intentionally limited to:

- Modernizing the GSE display interface to improve competitive positioning and technician usability
- Updating the Gen 3 control board only as required to support HVPS communication and dynamic power allocation
- Preserving the use of SkyLink kits as the primary mechanism for cloud telemetry and connectivity

This effort is not a communications platform redesign. It's a targeted interface modernization and system-integration initiative.

Name: GSED1.2-Core Objectives
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
1. Product Modernization
Improve the visual presentation and perceived innovation of the GSE product line to address competitive pressure and support sales efforts.

2. Technician Usability Improvement

Name: 1.0 Overview
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
This section defines the core user and business needs that the MHE comms solution must enable, incorporating native communications, telemetry, and digital enablement directly into the charger controller.
Originally scoped as a cross-platform �Platform Comms� add-on module intended to serve both GSE and MHE products, this effort has been intentionally narrowed and refocused based on leadership and engineering direction. The current scope is to deliver a cost-optimized, MHE-specific solution embedded directly into the ProCore Edge control board, rather than implemented as an external communications add-on.
This shift is driven by three core objectives:
- Cost reduction and scalability � Enable a connected ProCore Edge platform at a cost point that supports volume MHE deployments and commercial viability.
- System reliability and simplicity � Eliminate external comms modules in favor of a control board architecture that reduces wiring, thermal risk, service complexity, and long-term maintenance burden.
- Strategic digital enablement � Provide the hardware foundation required for Unified Portal connectivity, load and energy management, OTA updates, diagnostics, and long-term software evolution.

Name: 1.1 Context
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
This project is a hardware and system-architecture program, not solely a SW or cloud initiative. While it directly enables Unified Portal functionality, load management services, and future digital offerings, the primary output of this effort is a new ProCore Edge control board design that embeds communications, processing, storage, and security capabilities into the charger�s core control system.
Key program constraints and dependencies include:
- The solution is specific to MHE Charger platforms (PCE & PD) and is not intended to serve as a universal cross-portfolio comms module.
- Engineering is permitted to modify the ProCore Edge control board architecture to achieve the required cost, performance, and integration goals.
- The solution must align with and support the Unified Portal backend, which will serve as the primary telemetry, OTA, and device-management system.
- The design must be compatible with the ProCore Edge cabinet redesign effort, including enclosure, thermal, regulatory, and manufacturing considerations.
The purpose of this document is to formalize the market, product, and system requirements that ENG will use to develop the next-generation ProCore Edge controller. These requirements are intended to define capabilities, constraints, and outcomes (not to prescribe a specific implementation) so that ENG can evaluate architecture options and propose the most effective technical solution. A separate ENG requirements document should be created for further ENG specification.

Name: Secure Provisioning and Identification
Author: SpencerSkelly

Name: Power Budget and Thermal Impact
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:

This includes:
- Peak load scenarios (cellular + logging + OTA + control)
- High-temperature cabinet conditions
- Brownout and transient behavior

Name: OTA - Software Versioning & Rollback Capabilities
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
The system shall support version-controlled firmware updates with an option to rollback to previous stable versions if a failure occurs. The system shall support:

- Verification of update integrity before installation
- Monitoring of update status (queued, in progress, completed, failed)
- Automatic failure detection
- Rollback to last-known-good versions
- Prevention of device bricking

The system shall enable visibility into:
- Which devices are on which versions
-Devices requiring recovery action

Name: Session-Based & Periodic Data Uploads (Batched)
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
The system shall support batched or periodic upload of non-critical telemetry, including:

- Charge session summaries (energy delivered, timestamps, durations, vehicle/battery IDs)
- Configuration snapshots

This data shall be transmitted based on:
- End-of-event triggers (end of charge session)
- Configurable periodic intervals
- Manual/on-demand requests from the backend

Name: 1.0 Overview
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
The ProCore Edge enclosure redesign is a strategic cost-down and platform ownership initiative, not a cosmetic redesign.
Today, PosiCharge purchases fully assembled ProCore Edge cabinets from Delta Electronics. While Delta-s power modules are cost-effective on a $/kW basis, the cabinet and mechanical system are over-engineered, expensive, and are the primary driver of low contribution margin across the ProCore Edge line.
In parallel, Ampure acquired Power Designers (Florida), which designs and manufactures its own industrial charger enclosures. Power Designers consistently outperforms Ampure on contribution margin despite using more expensive power modules, largely due to low-cost, internally owned cabinet designs and localized manufacturing.
The goal of this project is to:
-	Establish a PosiCharge-owned ProCore Edge enclosure platform
-	Shift cabinet manufacturing from Delta Electronics to Power Designers (FL)
-	Continue sourcing Delta power modules only
-	Materially improve contribution margin, supply chain control, and scalability
-	Create a cabinet architecture capable of supporting future product growth across MHE and adjacent markets.
This redesign is intended to become the long-term mechanical foundation for the ProCore Edge product family.

Author: SpencerSkelly

Author: SpencerSkelly

Author: SpencerSkelly

Author: SpencerSkelly

Name: Bluetooth Data Download
Author: SpencerSkelly

Name: Bluetooth SW Update
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The Bluetooth interface shall support checking for available firmware updates and delivering the update package to the device's flash memory, completing the update transfer within 1 minute.

Name: Bluetooth Log Retrieval
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The Bluetooth interface shall support retrieval of all log types (device info, event, fault, EQ, configuration, diagnostic, connectivity, and asset logs) from the product to the connected device, completing retrieval of any single log type within 5 minutes.

Name: Bluetooth Product Status
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The Bluetooth interface shall transmit the current product operational status to the connected device in real time, including all of the following states: startup, unconnected, connected, charging, derated charging, fault, and maintenance.

Name: LAX_2025 I.a Procurement Description � eGSE Charging Equipment
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
Through this Request for Proposals (RFP), LAXTEC intends to procure a total of forty-eight (48) Fixed Charger Units and six (6) Mobile Charger Units, along with all related commissioning, delivery, and warranty services, to support electric ground support equipment (eGSE) operations at Los Angeles International Airport (LAX).
This procurement is being conducted in alignment with the requirements of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Voluntary Airport Low Emissions (VALE) Program. All equipment, materials, and services must comply with FAA Advisory Circular 150/5370-10 and other applicable federal, state, and local codes. Products must be eligible for reimbursement under FAA VALE guidelines, including adherence to Buy American Preferences as applicable.
The scope of work includes the furnishing, delivery, and commissioning of the following equipment:
Thirty-eight (38) eGSE Fixed Chargers
Stationary chargers to be installed at designated ramp locations. Each charger shall support electric ground service equipment charging, and be suitable for 24/7 operation in airport environments, and include integrated cable management and safety interlocks.
Ten (10) Level 3 Fixed Chargers
Stationary chargers to be installed at designated ramp locations. Capable of high- speed DC fast chargers designed for rapid charging of high-capacity eGSE and electric vehicles, and be suitable for 24/7 operation in airport environments, and include integrated cable management and safety interlocks..
Six (6) Mobile Charger Units
Portable, trailer-mounted or wheeled chargers capable of being deployed to multiple gates or service areas.
It is anticipated that all equipment will be furnished in Q3 2026. Equipment shall be delivered to LAX in accordance with the project schedule and packaged to prevent damage during transport.
The vendor shall provide commissioning services, including on-site testing, functional verification, and user training. A minimum two (2) year warranty shall be provided for all charger units and associated components. The warranty must include parts, labor, and remote support coverage for the full duration of the term.
In addition, proposers shall provide separate pricing for an optional extended warranty covering up to a total of five (5) years, inclusive of the required base warranty period. The extended warranty must provide the same level of coverage as the base warranty, including parts, labor, and remote support. Proposers may offer this extended warranty as annual renewals or as a bundled multi-year package.

Name: LAX_2025 II.b Description of the Terminals eGSE Chargers will be Procured For Tom Bradley International Terminal (TBIT)
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: TBIT is a full-service passenger terminal, designated primarily as a common use international facility. TBIT houses the Airport�s primary Federal Inspection Services facility (FIS). It is located between Terminals 3 and 4. The Terminal features various facilities for airlines and passengers, including international and domestic baggage claim facilities, ticketing counters, a security checkpoint, baggage screening and baggage make up areas, a range of concessions for shopping and dining, passenger hold rooms, and 19 gates that support 41 passenger boarding bridges, complete with fixed aircraft and ground support equipment, including pre-conditioned air, potable water, and ground power. TBIT also hosts a bus depot located at the north end of the concourse for transporting passengers between terminals. There are more than 40 airlines operating from TBIT on a regular basis to major international destinations. TBIT consists of five primary levels: the Departure Level (Level 4), which also houses various administrative offices; the Ticketing Level (Level 3); the Arrival Level (Level 1); and two sub-levels�Sub-Level 1, which includes the passenger tunnel to the MSC, and Sub-Level 2, which contains the baggage tunnels. Name: LAX_2025 II.c TBIT West Gates (formerly Mid-Field Satellite Concourse / MSC)

Note: TBIT West Gates is a passenger concourse which serves both domestic and international arrivals and departures. After clearing TBIT security, passengers access the TBIT West Gates via an underground passenger tunnel from TBIT or may otherwise arrive by bus from Terminal 1.5. Inbound international passengers are securely routed to the FIS while the facilities� domestic inbound passengers may exit the facility directly to domestic baggage claim on the lower level of TBIT, or transit back to Terminal 1.5 by bus. The TBIT West Gates Concourse is located just west of TBIT. The Terminal features various facilities for airlines and passengers, including a baggage make up area, a range of concessions for shopping and dining, passenger hold rooms, and 15 gates that support 27 passenger boarding bridges, complete with fixed aircraft and ground support equipment, including pre-conditioned air, potable water, and ground power. The concourse also hosts a bus depot located central to the concourse for transporting passengers between terminals. There are more than 20 airlines operating from TBIT on a weekly basis to major domestic and international destinations. Name: LAX_2025 II.a Description of LAXTEC
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
The Los Angeles International Airport Equipment Company (�LAXTEC�) is an airline consortium organized as a California not-for-profit mutual benefit corporation. LAXTEC supports more than 50 member and non-member airlines operating across multiple terminals and concourses throughout Los Angeles International Airport (LAX). The organization is responsible for the operations and maintenance of designated facilities, equipment, and systems, and for providing a range of airline, aircraft, and airport maintenance and support services to its member airlines, the City of Los Angeles, and the Airport.
LAXTEC currently provides services across multiple LAX areas, including Terminal 1.5, Terminal 5, Tom Bradley International Terminal (TBIT), the TBIT West Gates (formerly the Midfield Satellite Concourse/MSC), Terminal 6, and the Far-West Remote Gate Concourse. Limited services are provided at Terminal 2 and Terminal 7. No services are currently provided at LAX Cargo, the South Pad, B1 Pad, or C1 Pad.

Name: LAX_2025 II.g LAX Cargo
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The LAX Cargo facilities are comprised of multiple on-airport cargo terminals and warehouses located along the northern and southern perimeters of the airfield. These facilities support air cargo operations, including freight handling, customs clearance, aircraft parking, and ground handling. Cargo operations are conducted by various freight carriers, ground handlers, and logistics companies. The cargo area also includes tenant-leased office spaces, vehicle parking, and access to aircraft stands for narrow-body and wide-body cargo aircraft.

Event Notification Preferences:

Name: CC111 Audit Trail - Configuration Changes

Name: CC112 Backwards Compatibility with Existing Systems
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The updated Gen IV Control/Comms system shall be fully backward compatible with all existing GSE power stations. The Gen IV system must seamlessly integrate into old systems, ensuring that customers can upgrade by replacing only the front door panel or the control/comms board.

Name: CC113 Future-Proof Architecture for Next-Gen Systems
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The Gen IV Control/Comms Board shall be designed to support future system integrations, including but not limited to: next-generation high-voltage chargers, connection to mobile devices/apps, and expanded API functionalities.

Name: CC114 Redundancy for Critical Data Storage & Uptime
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The system shall implement local redundancy for data storage, ensuring that critical logs (faults, energy usage, diagnostics) are not lost in the event of system crashes or memory corruption.

Name: CC101 Charger Registration - Cloud Portal
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note:
The system shall provide a means of registering chargers in the cloud portal, similar to vehicle asset registration. This process shall allow users to register the charger with the following details: 
- Charger Serial Number
- Charger ID
- Charger Model and Generation
- Site/Location
-Registration Date
- Firmware Version & Software Version

Name: CC102 Configure Charger + Gen IV Board - Display

Name: CC105 Security - Configuration Access
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The system shall enforce secure login protocols for accessing configuration options which are a security risk, (e.g., password/PIN protection, two-factor authentication) preventing unauthorized changes to critical charger or control board settings. For fields that are a security risk, the system shall only allow authorized personnel to make changes.

Name: CC106 Save Configuration Settings to Backend
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The system shall save all configuration settings (e.g., network connectivity, charger parameters, serial number associations, etc.) to the backend for future reference and validation.

Name: CC107 Save Charger Information to Backend
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The system shall save all key charger information (e.g.,  firmware version, SW version, charger serial number, last maintenance date, last connected/contact date, etc.) to the backend for future reference and validation.

Name: CC108 Charger Parameter Configuration (On Site)
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note:
The system shall allow installers and maintenance technicians to configure the following parameters on-site via the display, mobile app, or laptop:
- Charger ID
- Gen IV Control Board Serial Number to match Charger Serial ID
- EQ Settings (enable/disable Auto EQ, EQ button)
- Charging Parameters (state of charge, full charge setup, derate charger, etc.)
- Temperature Readout Settings
- Daylight Savings Time Adjustments
- Date and Time Settings

Name: CC94 Personnel Safety Features
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The physical installation process for the Gen IV Control/Comms board shall include built-in personnel safety features such as clear lockout-tagout instructions, proper grounding mechanisms, and visual indicators for live connections.

Name: CC95 Installation Verification
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The system shall enable installers to test connections and confirm functionality post-installation. This verification shall include indicators on the display or cloud portal confirming successful setup.

Name: CC96 Physical Installation Guides and Documentation
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The Gen IV Control/Comms board shall have comprehensive, step-by-step installation guides and clear labeling on connectors, ensuring ease of installation for technicians. This shall include physical manuals and online resources with visual aids.

Name: CC97 Factory Pre-Configuration of Serial Numbers and Charger IDs
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The Gen IV Control/Comms Board shall support factory pre-configuration of the Control Board Serial Number and the Charger ID to match the physical charger they are paired with before leaving the factory.

Name: CC98 Verify Data Points at Factory
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The system shall enable verification of pre-configured data points (e.g., serial number, charger ID, default configurations) at the factory to ensure accuracy before shipping.

Name: CC99 Configure Network Connectivity at Factory
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The Gen IV Control/Comms Board shall support factory pre-configuration of network settings, including WiFi  and cellular options, based on client requirements.

Name: CC100 Assign Gen IV Control Board Parameters at Factory
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The factory shall support configuration of parameters such as date, time, and charger-specific settings (e.g., energy thresholds) to minimize on-site adjustments.

Name: CC87 Network Security and Access Control
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The system shall implement secure protocols (e.g., WPA3 for Wi-Fi, SSL for remote connections) and require password-protected access to network configuration interfaces to prevent unauthorized changes.

Name: CC88 Testing and Validation of Network Connectivity
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The system shall include/allow for a means of testing to validate network connectivity after configuration, ensuring the charger is operational before leaving the site.

Name: CC89 Modular Upgrade Options
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note:
The Gen IV Control/Comms system shall allow customers to choose between:
- Purchasing the full system (new front door panel with Gen IV board and updated display).
- Purchasing only the Gen IV Control/Comms board for replacement within the existing system.

Name: CC90 Operational Independence of Control and Comms (Functionality)
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The Gen IV Control/Comms system shall ensure operational independence between the control and comms functions. In the event of a comms failure, the charger shall continue to operate without disruption.

Name: CC91 Independent Serviceability of Control and Comms Boards
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The Gen IV Control/Comms system shall allow independent servicing of the control and comms boards. Replacing or repairing one board must not affect the functionality or integrity of the other.

Name: CC92 Durability - System Panel & Display Design
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The Gen IV front door panel shall be designed for robustness, able to withstand harsh handling, environmental exposure, and operational wear-and-tear. Materials shall meet NEMA 3R (North America) and IP55 (CE) standards for ingress protection against dust and water.

Name: CC93 Modular Connectors for Simplified Installation
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The Gen IV Control/Comms board shall use modular connectors with distinct shapes and sizes to reduce wiring errors during installation. Connections shall be color-coded, labeled, and keyed to their respective ports to ensure proper attachment.

Name: CC81 Integrations - API Only Access
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: Data access by third-party integrations shall only be permitted via a secure API, ensuring that external systems / unauthorized agents cannot extract data directly from the charger hardware.

Name: 10 Network Connectivity & Configuration
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: Configuring network connectivity for the Gen IV Control/Comms system must be designed to simplify and streamline the process compared to the current Skylink solution. The requirements must focus on making the system usable, secure, and efficient for installers and fleet managers, ensuring it meets market expectations for reliability and ease of deployment.

Name: CC82 Support for Multiple Network Protocols
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note:
The system shall support configuration for multiple network protocols, including:
- Ethernet: Ensure active connection detection.
- Wi-Fi: Allow input of SSID and password.
- Cellular: Validate SIM card credentials and include multi-carrier SIM (domestic + international support)
- Serial Port: Provide fallback for configuration in cases where other methods fail.
- Bluetooth: Enable secure and quick setup during initial configuration.

Name: CC83 Intuitive Network Configuration Process
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note:
The system shall provide an intuitive interface for network configuration. Including:
- Auto-detection of available network protocols and prioritization based on speed and reliability.
- Real-time feedback for successful or failed connection attempts, with clear error messages (e.g., "Invalid credentials," "Network unavailable").

Name: CC84 Transition Between Network Modes
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The system shall allow seamless transition between network modes (e.g., switching from Wi-Fi to cellular) without requiring a full reconfiguration. In addition, switching between network modes shall not result in critical data loss or significant system downtime.

Name: CC85 Offline Operation and Configuration
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The system shall continue to function without network connectivity and store critical configuration locally. Offline configurations must automatically sync with the backend when connectivity is restored.

Name: CC86 Diagnostics and Troubleshooting for Connectivity Issues
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note:
The system shall provide tools to diagnose and troubleshoot connectivity issues, including:
- Viewing communication logs for error patterns.
- Running diagnostics tests for each network protocol.
These options shall be available both for on-site diagnostics and remote troubleshooting.

Name: CC74 Support for ISO 15118 (Plug & Charge & V2G)
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The system shall support ISO 15118, enabling vehicle-to-charger communication for  authentication, we well as the potential for future bidirectional energy transfer (V2G - Vehicle-to-Grid).

Name: CC75 Support for CAN Communication
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note:
The system shall support CAN Bus protocols to ensure direct communication with industrial vehicles and lithium  battery management systems (BMS), enabling better data exchange and real-time diagnostics.

Name: CC76 Support for Bluetooth Communication
Author: ChescaLegaspi

Name: 1.1 Objective
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The Gen IV Control/Comms Board aims to replace the current Raspberry Pi auxiliary Skylink kit system with a fully integrated and streamlined solution, enhancing reliability, ease of use, and scalability. This project will focus on improving diagnostic capabilities, connectivity, and configurability for maintenance technicians and fleet managers.

Name: 1.2 Scope
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The Gen IV Control/Comms board will replace the existing Raspberry Pi Skylink kits by embedding communication, diagnostics, and control capabilities directly into the system. The system will support use cases for maintenance technicians, fleet managers, and operational teams, focusing on enhanced diagnostics, asset management, and real-time telemetry.

Name: 1.3 Context
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note: The current auxiliary Skylink kit system requires a Raspberry Pi mounted externally, leading to frequent reliability issues and increased field maintenance costs. Moving to an integrated solution resolves these challenges while reducing operational complexity.

Name: 1.4 Target Audience
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note:
The primary users of the Gen IV Control/Comms Board are:
- Maintenance Technicians: On-site personnel conducting diagnostics and troubleshooting.
- Fleet Managers: Remote users monitoring and managing multiple assets via software portals. (Asset Registration, Energy Reporting, Remote Access)
- Energy/Utility Partners: Stakeholders requiring system-level energy management and reporting capabilities.

Name: 1.5 Key Feature Overview
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note:
The Gen IV board shall enable the following key features:
- Diagnostics: Enhanced on-site and remote fault analysis.
- Connectivity: Support for Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and cellular communication.
- Asset Management: Simplified asset registration, authorization, and tracking
- Energy Reporting: Full reporting for individual and bulk assets, Enable customers to track asset energy usage or bill for energy.
- Configuration Tools: More intuitive interfaces for configuration.

Name: 1.6 Value Proposition
Author: ChescaLegaspi
Note:
The transition to an integrated Gen IV Control/Comms Board aligns with customer demand for reliability and scalability while addressing pain points associated with the current auxiliary Skylink kit. Value propositions include:
- Improvde system reliability and reduced downtime.
- Simplified hardware architecture, Streamline maintenance and reduce costs.
- Enable full integration of diagnostics, configuration, and asset management into a single control system.
- Reduce dependency on auxiliary hardware, increasing scalability.

Beginning in 2007, most of the U.S. will begin Daylight Saving Time at 2:00 a.m. on the second Sunday in March and revert to standard time on the first Sunday in November. In the U.S., each time zone switches at a different time. 
In the European Union, Summer Time begins and ends at 1:00 a.m. Universal Time (Greenwich Mean Time). It begins the last Sunday in March and ends the last Sunday in October. In the EU, all time zones change at the same moment. [http://webexhibits.org/daylightsaving/b.html]

Name: GSE_SW 2.4.4.1 Comm PowerServer
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The Comm PowerServer interface consists of a point-to-point RS422 data link.  This is a full-duplex dual twisted pair arrangement to eliminate the need for signal drive control; TX and RX drives are always active.  By utilizing off-the-shelf RS232 to RS422 converters it is very easy to adapt any COM port equipped devices to this link. The PowerServer communicates with the Master PowerStation, continuously updating it as to faults and power available.

Name: GSE_SW 2.9.3.1 Selector Mode [Not implemented at this time]
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
The Selector Mode is used to provide the capability to command the charger, via the serial communication port, to open and close relays on the charger control board.  The relays can be used to control external accessories, such as lights. 
One example of the use of Selector Mode is the Truck Selector.  In the Truck Selector application, Selector Mode is used to support turning a green or red light on to indicate which trucks are charged to a sufficient SOC for use, and which are not.  The external system commands the charger to illuminate the green light and extinguish the red light for the trucks that are ready for use.  The external system commands the charger to illuminate the red light and extinguish the green light for trucks that need to remain charging.  All decision making is performed external to the charger.

Name: GSE_SW 2.7.1 Watering
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
The MVS/DVS system provides a means of controlling an external watering system to support battery maintenance.  The system includes controlling pre-defined systems, as well as offering a custom mode to control systems not currently defined in the system. 
Watering is accomplished during EQ charging as configured in the Charger Configuration Watering Control Menu (see section 2.8.1.2.11).  The charger’s watering functionality includes enabling a relay to control the external watering system, for a configured duration, at the appropriate time during the EQ charge.

Name: GSE_SW 1.3.22. Power Allocation
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The Power Allocation Algorithm allows for the maximal use of the power being delivered to the PowerStations by the PowerServer. This Algorithm allocates the power based on the SOC of the batteries currently charging as well as their charging states. Based on priorities, a certain percentage of the power being requested is allocated to the Port requesting the power. In general, power is allocated in proportion to the degree of discharge of a battery. If the available power is inadequate to supply all connected batteries, the needs of the lowest batteries are satisfied first. The priorities are continually recalculated and power is reallocated when the priorities change.

Name: GSE_SW 1.1 Purpose
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
The PowerStation is one of two primary components of the AeroVironment Dual Vehicle Charging Systems (DVS) and the Multiple Vehicle Charging Systems (MVS).  These systems provide fast charging technology and intelligent power management for charging multiple vehicles.  
The three primary components of the systems are the PowerServer, the PowerStation and the Battery Monitor/Identification (BMID) unit.  
The PowerServer functions as the utility line rectifier, converting the 3-phase power to DC power for the PowerStations. In the original MVS, up to 5 dual-port PowerStations, can be connected in a daisy chain manner to the DC bus of a single Communications (Comm) PowerServer, allowing up to 10 vehicles to charge simultaneously. In the NGPS MVS System up to 8 dual-port PowerStations can be connected to the DC bus, allowing p to 16 vehicles to charge simultaneously. 
The Dual Vehicle System (DVS) contains an integrated PowerServer mounted below a PowerStation.  The 33kW and 40kW versions of the DVS can have up to 3 additional PowerStations connected to the DC bus, allowing up to 8 vehicles to charge simultaneously.  The 30kW version is limited to charging 2 vehicles simultaneously. 
Each PowerStation has two DC-to-DC converters to convert the PowerServer DC bus to the desired output value.  Vehicles request power for charging as determined by the BMID. 
Each PowerStation is capable of simultaneously charging two 80-volt Battery packs at a rate of 250/320 amps, limited only by the power available from the PowerServer. With a single vehicle connected, the PowerStation is capable of providing up to 500 amps to the connected port.  
In each system a Master PowerStation is assigned the task of allocating the power from the PowerServer.  
In the original MVS, the Comm PowerServer and Master PowerStation are linked via a serial interface.  This communication interface is used to share diagnostic information between the two units as well as exchange operating commands.  
In the NGPS MVS System and the DVS systems, the Master PowerStation commands the PowerServer to start outputting power through the use of relay closures. 
The purpose of this document is to describe the High Level Software Requirements for the PowerStation.  The requirements for the Comm Server serial communications are also documented here for historical purposes.

Name: GSE_SW 2.2 Charge Handling
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The charge handler is designed to implement an AV standard industrial Fast Charge algorithm.  This is based on a typical Constant Current - Constant Voltage - Constant Current profile with provisions to maximize fast charge performance and battery life.  In addition to Fast Charging, the system will also provide a means to Equalize a battery.  The steps involved with charging are broken into charge states: Idle, Fast Charge, Full, Equalization Charge and Abnormal Termination states. These states apply to both Port A and Port B.

Name: GSE_SW 2.2.1 Charger States
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
The charge handler implements a standard charge protocol by progressing from one state to another using transition checks along the way.  The charge state mapping is shown in Figure 2-3. 
The data for the charging algorithms comes from four places: the BMID attached to the battery (Battery configuration, voltage and temperature), the charger inputs (current, voltage and connection status), the charger configuration parameters, and the charging tables (see [11]).  The request to charge comes from the system state machine.  Once started, the charging handler progresses through the charging states until it terminates either normally or abnormally. 
The first states of charging are for charge initialization.  By default, if no charge is requested the system waits in the Disconnected state.  Once a battery is connected and the system determines that a charge can be started, charging proceeds to the next states. If the BMID, battery, and charger data all fall into usable ranges then the charging progresses to the PowerStage preparation, charging and termination states.

Name: GSE_SW 2.1 User Interface
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The user interface processes inputs from the analog-to-digital converter driver, BMID handler, charge handler, charge log handler, fault handler, fault log handler, LED driver, RTC handler, and system state handler.  Status information is output to the user display, LEDs and serial port.  User requests for data, via the serial port, are also processed by the user interface.

Name: GSE_SW 2.10 Charger Display Screens
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The charger display screens contain specific information pertaining to the charger and batteries that have been charged or are currently being charged.  The menus and sub-menus contain specific information and configurable parameters data that are used to tailor the charging process.

Name: GSE_SW 2.9 PosiNET Software Requirements
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The charger broadcasts real time data for collection and processing by an external resource, such as a stand-alone PC.  The broadcast data consists of charger and BMID real-time data.  The charger also transmits log data when requested by an external resource.  The Master PowerStation can be configured to collects log data from it’s own activities as well as from all Slave PowerStations in the networked system.  The log data consists of the charge events, fault events and BMID data collected by the charger (see section 2.6).

Name: GSE_SW 2.3 Fault Handling
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The fault handler collects, filters, and processes errors into either warnings or faults.  The fault handler is used to implement hysterisis on system errors that come from external handlers.  Some errors that are considered fatal will set faults and never clear, while others will clear themselves as soon as the cause for the error condition ceases.
