Author: SpencerSkelly

Name: UL 2202 53.11
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: 53.11 For the loading conditions, a variable resistor is to be connected across the secondary winding. Each test described in 53.1 (a) - (c) is to be continued until a risk of fire develops, the 3-ampere fuse opens, a winding of the transformer or a protective device opens or 15 days have passed. In conducting the tests described in 53.1 (a) - (c), the variable resistance load is to be adjusted to the required value as quickly as possible and readjusted, where required 1 minute after voltage is applied to the primary winding. For a switch-mode transformer, the load is to be connected to the output of the power supply connected to the transformer.

Name: UL 2202 53.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
53.1 Except as noted in 53.2, a flanged bobbin transformer required to be tested as provided in (c) of 27.2.4 � also see 27.2.7 � shall operate for 15 days with the secondary winding or windings loaded to the conditions described below in (a) � (c). A risk of fire or electric shock shall not result from:
a) Short-circuiting the secondary winding;
b) Loading the secondary winding to a current equal to maximum normal current plus X percent of the difference between the short-circuit current and the rated current � where X equals 75, 50, 25, 20, 15, 10, and 5, respectively; and
c) Loading the secondary winding to maximum normal current.

Name: UL 2202 58.3
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: 58.3 When the fuse or circuit protective device is used to protect more than one secondary winding or taps, each winding or partial winding is to be tested as indicated in 58.1 or 58.2 with the remaining windings delivering rated load.

Name: UL 2202 56.3
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: 56.3 The cable clamp shall be held firmly in place. A force equivalent to the pressure of 1.034 N/mm2 (150 lb/in2) times the cross sectional area of the EV cable [rounded up to the nearest 22.2 N (5 lb) increment], but not less than 156 N (35 lbs), shall be applied gradually to the EV cable at a point not less than 150 mm (6 inches) from the cable grip in a direction perpendicular to the plane of the opening and in line with the cable. The force shall be applied and sustained for one minute.

Name: UL 2202 53.9
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: 53.9 To determine whether a transformer complies with the requirement in 53.1, three separate samples are to be subjected to each condition described in 53.1 (a) - (c). For a transformer that employs more than one secondary winding, each of the secondary windings is to be loaded for each condition specified in 53.1 with the other windings loaded to rated current. The test conditions are to be as described in 53.10 � 53.14.

Name: UL 2202 59.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: 59.1 In accordance with the requirement in 14.1.2.8, an insulating base or support and the bus or strap upon which pressure wire connectors for field wiring are mounted shall be subjected to the force created when the connectors, securing short lengths of conductors sized as described in 14.1.1.4, are torqued to 125 % of the value marked on the unit. The results meet the intent of the requirement when the base is not damaged as defined in 59.2. The test is not required for wire connectors that are part of a component such as a terminal block, circuit breaker, switch, or similar device.

Name: UL 2202 56.4
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: 56.4 A torque shall also be applied to the EV cable at a point 150 mm (6 inches) from the cable grip as specified in Table 56.1 for one minute in the direction least favorable to the clamp construction.

Name: UL 2202 53.14

Note: 53.14 When a protective device opens the circuit or a winding on any sample opens during the 15-day abnormal-operation tests while the samples are unattended, the variable resistor load on the other samples is to be increased, by reducing the resistance, until the protective device opens the circuit or the winding opens, so that the samples are subjected to the dielectric voltage-withstand test described in 53.5 while in a heated condition. 1. power up system > plug in vehicle > AC contactor closes > adjust network configuration settings => AC contactor should open
2. power up system > adjust network configuration settings => AC contactor should remain open
3. power up system > plug in vehicle > AC contactor closes > create fault => AC contactor should open

BYD/CAN Improvement	Check that voltage reported by CAN bus is processed without a delay that affects charging. Charge with BYD battery. Record CAN traces.

Name: EN 1175 4.3.3 Protection from ingress of water and dust
Note:
4.3.3 Protection from ingress of water and dust
The electrical installation of the trucks in operating condition shall be designed and constructed such that the protection from harmful ingress of water and dust is in accordance with the environmental conditions in which the truck is designed to operate, including reasonably foreseeable misuses, as defined in the instruction handbook (see EN ISO 3691-1:2015, 6.2.2).
NOTE Standardised degrees of protection provided by the enclosure of the electrical equipment are given in EN 60529:1991.

Name: EN 1175 4.3.2 Frame fault
Note:
4.3.2 Frame fault
The electric circuits shall be so designed or protected, that frame faults shall not cause hazardous inadvertent movements that cannot be corrected or compensated by the operator. Compliance shall be verified by means of the type test of 4.10.4.

Name: EN 1175 4.3.9 Sparking or heat dissipating electrical components
Note:
4.3.9 Sparking or heat dissipating electrical components
Sparking components and components which can reach a temperature of 300 �C or more under normal operating conditions, shall not be located where potentially explosive gas/air mixtures can be present. Battery connectors shall be accepted as non-sparking components if they are not used as an emergency switching-off device.

Name: EN 1175 4.3.1 Low voltage/high voltage
Note:
4.3.1 Low voltage/high voltage
Safety shall not be compromised at any voltage level that can occur.
Electrical systems of trucks powered by lead-acid batteries shall be designed so that all functions operate in the voltage range from 70 % up to 120 % of the nominal battery voltage. These limits shall be adapted to other energy sources technologies by the manufacturer.
NOTE Limits set by the manufacturer for other energy sources are outside the scope of this document.

Name: EN 1175 4.3.8 Fire and heat hazards (installation of arcing and sparking parts)
Note:
4.3.8 Fire and heat hazards (installation of arcing and sparking parts)
Any arcing part in a power circuit shall be enclosed or installed to adequately reduce the possibility of flame or molten material causing a risk of fire.
Relevant parts shall be accessible for servicing and inspection.

Name: EN 1175 4.7.2.2 Unintended steering movements
Note:
4.7.2.2 Unintended steering movements
A single electrical/electronic fault shall not lead to a risk of an unintended operation caused by the steering system.
Within 0,1 s from the start of an unintended steering movement:
a) on trucks not provided with backup steering, the fault shall be detected, the stop of the unintended steering operation and a controlled stop shall be initiated;
b) on trucks provided with backup steering, the fault shall be detected, the stop of the unintended steering operation shall be initiated, the backup steering system shall be activated automatically.
These safety functions shall be in accordance with PLr shown in Table 4.

Name: EN 1175 4.10.3.3 Insulation resistance of battery
Note:
4.10.3.3 Insulation resistance of battery
The insulation resistance of the disconnected, filled and charged traction battery mounted on the truck shall be at least 500 ? multiplied by the nominal voltage of the truck system between the live parts and the frame of the truck. Where the battery is fitted into more than one container this test shall be carried out with the sections (including metal battery containers) electrically connected.

Name: EN 1175 Table 4 - Performance levels of steering systems
EN 1175 4.3.10.2 External radiation
Note:
4.3.10.2 External radiation
Operation of trucks shall not be hazardously influenced by external radiation and for that purpose trucks shall at least comply with EN 12895:2015+A1:2019, 4.2, 5.1 and 5.3.
NOTE For detailed information regarding electromagnetic compatibility refer to EN 12895:2015+A1:2019.

Name: EN 1175 4.3.4 Protection against electric shock
Note:
4.3.4 Protection against electric shock
Non-insulated live parts of trucks in the operating condition shall be protected to a degree of IPXXB preventing direct contact. For top surfaces, the minimum degree shall be IPXXD in accordance with EN 60529:1991.
Access to an electrical enclosure containing uninsulated live parts in excess of nominal voltage 60 V DC or 25 V AC shall be possible only using a tool.
Indirect contact with live parts shall be avoided by electric separation of the protection devices in accordance with EN 60204-1:2006, 6.3.2.3.
It shall be possible to electrically disconnect the energy sources for maintenance and replacement operations. An easily accessible switch, connector or disconnectable battery terminals meets the intent of this requirement.
For energy sources with nominal voltage greater than 60 V DC or 25 V AC live parts shall be protected against direct contact.

Name: EN 1175 4.3.10.1 Non-ionising radiation
Note:
4.3.10.1 Non-ionising radiation
Where trucks are fitted with non-ionising radiation devices related to the operation of the truck, the radiation shall be minimized with consideration to the influence on persons, in particular with the effect on active or non-active implantable medical devices  by complying with EN 12895:2015+A1:2019, 4.1, 5.1 and 5.2.

Name: EN 1175 4.10.2.1 General
Note:
4.10.2.1 General
The insulation test shall be applied to battery driven trucks with traction battery disconnected and to IC trucks equipped with electric power transmission systems.
The insulation resistance of the truck and traction battery shall be checked separately.
Test voltage can be either DC or AC. DC test voltage shall be greater than 50 V. AC test voltage shall be greater than 35 VRMS.

Name: EN 1175 4.9.2.2 Assistance systems
Note:
4.9.2.2 Assistance systems
Assistance systems shall conform to Annex E.

Name: EN 1175 4.8.3 Parameters
Note:
4.8.3 Parameters
Uncontrolled change of the electronic system parameters shall not lead to hazardous situations. The probability of storage device faults that can affect the change of the critical parameters shall be included in the calculation of the PL of the corresponding safety function
Any change of parameter values controlled by the operator shall not result in a hazardous situation.
Parameter modification outside the range permitted to the operator shall conform to EN ISO 13849-1:2015, 4.6.4.

Name: EN 1175 4.7.2.1 General
Note:
4.7.2.1 General
Electrical/electronic steering control systems shall be designed to avoid hazardous deviations not controllable by the operator.

Name: EN 1175 4.10.2.2 Insulation of truck
Note:
4.10.2.2 Insulation of truck
The test voltage shall be applied between the truck frame and each active part of the power circuits. The elements of these active parts may be tested in common if they are connected by low impedance circuits, e.g. by the free-wheeling diodes of a converter or the motor windings.
The insulation resistance between the active parts of the power circuits and the frame shall be at least 1 000 ? multiplied by the nominal voltage of the truck system.
The test shall be repeated if electric components connected to the electric power circuits are installed subsequently.
10 For instance, low power auxiliary circuits are: electronic control systems for lamps or wiper motors, cooling fans, etc.
11 Frequency between 25 Hz and 100 Hz.

Name: EN 1175 4.9.2.3 Electrical coupling control for towing
Note:
4.9.2.3 Electrical coupling control for towing
The following additional requirements shall apply to devices for towing in accordance with EN ISO 3691-1:2015, 4.12:
a) Unintended decoupling caused by a fault of the electric/electronic system shall be avoided. This safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 6.
b) Decoupling of the trailer by the operator while travelling shall be avoided. This safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 6.
c) The control device for the operator shall be recognizable and measures shall be taken against unintended activation.

Name: EN 1175 4.6.6 Limitation of load movement functions
Note:
4.6.6 Limitation of load movement functions
Electrical/electronic speed - and/or position - control and limitation systems shall be in accordance with the PLr shown in Table 3.
For limitation of load movement as operator assistance see Annex E.
An LHS limiting function shall be considered a safety function if it is required for passing the truck stability type tests, e.g. tilting angle limitation, maximum reach of the mast, limitation of the side shift displacement.

Name: EN 1175 4.8.1 General
Note:
4.8.1 General
Safety-related embedded or application software shall be designed according to the requirements of EN ISO 13849-1:2015, 4.6.

Name: EN 1175 4.7.1 General
Note:
4.7.1 General
The hazards resulting from failures of electric or electric assisted steering systems are dependent on the type of the steering system. The following safety functions shall be applied to the corresponding steering system.
NOTE 1  To define when a redundant backup steering system in addition to electric steering is required is out of the scope of this document.

NOTE 2  Additional information about steering systems can be found in Annex F.

NOTE 3 Additional information regarding the correspondence between requirements of 4.7 and most common causes of hazard can be found in Annex J.

Name: EN 1175 4.9.2.1 Warning/indicator devices
Note:
4.9.2.1 Warning/indicator devices
Where the truck is fitted with warning/indicator devices, the output shall be unambiguous and easily perceived.
Where warning/indicator devices are part of a safety function they shall comply with the PLr of that function.
Where warning/indicator devices are not part of a safety function, means shall be provided to check the operation of such devices without the use of tools. If this check is intended to be carried out by the operator, the instruction manual shall contain the exact procedure.

Name: EN 1175 4.8.2 Symbols and languages for user interfaces, service interfaces and keypads
Note:
4.8.2 Symbols and languages for user interfaces, service interfaces and keypads
Symbols shall be in accordance with ISO 3287. When symbols do not exist in ISO 3287 for functions, alternative symbols shall be derived from ISO 7000 / IEC 60417.
If text is used in the interface, it shall be in the language(s) of the country in which the truck is to be used.
NOTE In addition, the manufacturer can at the request of the user provide the information in other language(s) understood by operators.

The information shall be readable in the intended working conditions.

Name: EN 1175 4.6.5 Load clamp devices
Note:
4.6.5 Load clamp devices
Trucks equipped with attachments which hold the load by power (for instance, paper clamps) shall feature controls with a secondary action to prevent unintentional release of the load in accordance with EN ISO 3691-1:2015, 4.4.4.1.
If the prevention of unintentional release is realized by an electric/electronic system this safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 3.

Name: EN 1175 4.10.3.2 Insulation resistance of truck
Note:
4.10.3.2 Insulation resistance of truck
The insulation resistance between live parts of all electric components and the frame of the industrial truck except for the battery shall be at least 1 000 ? multiplied by the nominal voltage of the truck system.

Name: EN 1175 4.9.3 Other safety functions
Note:
4.9.3 Other safety functions
This document specifies at Table 2, Table 3, Table 4 and Table 6 minimum required performance levels (PLr) for the common safety functions of industrial trucks realized by safety-related parts of control systems. While these PLr may give guidance for the determination of PLr for other safety functions, this would be outside the scope of this document.
NOTE PLr for other safety functions can be defined in other truck specific standards or determined by the manufacturer using risk assessment. Also, the following are considered a minimum for the three main hazards:

� Tipping over: PLr = c

� Unintended hazardous movement (drive system, LHS): PLr = c

� Unintended steering while driving: PLr = d

Name: EN 1175 4.9.1.2.1
Note: 4.9.1.2.1 In accordance with EN 60204-1:2006, 9.2.5.4.3 actuation of the emergency switching off control shall initiate within 0,2 s the stop of all potentially hazardous movements that are electrically/electronically powered or controlled. This safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 6.

Name: EN 1175 4.7.3 Electric powered assisted steering systems
Note:
4.7.3 Electric powered assisted steering systems
Any failure of the electrical part of an electric powered assisted steering system shall not prevent the truck from maintaining the path being steered.
A failure of the electric powered assisted steering system shall be signalled to the operator. This safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 4.
NOTE When a failure of the electrical part of an electric powered assisted steering system causes reduced steering performance, the truck may be automatically brought to one of the conditions defined in 4.5.1.

Name: EN 1175 4.9.1.1 Access
Note:
4.9.1.1 Access
An emergency switching off control or controls shall be provided which shall always be accessible to the operator whilst in any of the operating positions specified by the manufacturer.

Name: EN 1175 4.7.2.4 Backup steering warning
Note:
4.7.2.4 Backup steering warning
A single electrical/electronic fault as described in 4.7.2.2 and 4.7.2.3 on trucks provided with backup steering shall activate a warning to the operator.
This safety function shall be in accordance with PLr as defined in Table 4.

Name: EN 1175 4.6.4 Deviation from setpoint
Note:
4.6.4 Deviation from setpoint
The LHS shall be so designed that deviation from operator setpoint, caused by an electrical fault, which could result in hazardous truck movement is prevented.
The following behaviour is considered as hazardous:
a) movement from standstill, longer than a time of 0,2 s, without activating LHS controls;
b) unintended hazardous deviation from setpoint of an active LHS function. The level of deviation depends on the LHS function. Hazardous deviations are those deviations from setpoint that the operator is not able to control, and which lead to loss of load or stability.
For specific applications a time less than 0,2 s can be required, e.g. electric/electronic controlled load clamp devices.
These safety functions shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 3.

Name: EN 1175 4.10.3.1 General
Note:
4.10.3.1 General
The insulation test shall be applied to battery driven trucks with traction battery disconnected and to IC trucks equipped with electric power transmission systems.
The insulation resistance of the truck and traction battery shall be checked separately. The test voltage shall be greater than the nominal voltage up to a limit of 500 V.

Name: EN 1175 4.9.2.6 Unauthorised starting
Note:
4.9.2.6 Unauthorised starting
If trucks are provided with an electric/electronic control system for operator authorization in accordance with EN ISO 3691-1:2015, 4.2.1, e.g. key code unit or magnetic card, the safety function to prevent unauthorised starting shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 6.

Name: EN 1175 4.7.2.5 Deviation from setpoint
Note:
4.7.2.5 Deviation from setpoint
The steering control system shall detect potentially hazardous deviations between setpoint and actpoint.
Hazardous deviations are those deviations from setpoint that the operator is not able to control. In case of hazardous deviations, one of the conditions defined in 4.5.1 shall be initiated within 0,1 s.
This safety function shall be in accordance with PLr as defined in Table 4.

Name: EN 1175 4.10.2.3 Insulation of battery
Note:
4.10.2.3 Insulation of battery
The insulation resistance of the disconnected, filled and charged traction battery mounted on the truck shall be at least 50 ? multiplied by the nominal voltage of the truck system between the positive and negative pole of the battery and the frame of the truck. Where the battery is fitted into more than one container this test shall be carried out with the sections (including metal battery containers) electrically connected.

Name: EN 1175 4.9.2.4 Slack wire-ropes or chains
Note:
4.9.2.4 Slack wire-ropes or chains
Safety function detecting slack wire-ropes and chains and stopping movements on trucks designed to travel with elevated operator shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 6.

Name: EN 1175 4.7.2.3 Supervision of steering system
Note:
4.7.2.3 Supervision of steering system
An electrical/electronic fault potentially leading to loss of steering functions (for instance breakdown of steering controller or output stage, loss of power supply) shall on trucks:
a) without a backup steering system initiate a controlled stop; or
b) with backup (secondary) system initiate an automatic activation of the backup (secondary) system.
This safety function shall be in accordance with PLr shown in Table 4.
NOTE For additional information about steering systems see Annex F.

Name: EN 1175 4.6.3 Monitoring of operating position
Note:
4.6.3 Monitoring of operating position
On sit-on and stand-on trucks a separate device (OPC) independent of the LHS controls shall automatically bring an active LHS to a safe state, as defined in 4.6.1, if the operator leaves the normal operating position. Nuisance deactivation of the OPC due to operating conditions, such as rough ground, shall be prevented. The safe state shall be initiated not later than 2,0 s after deactivation of the OPC.
If the LHS function is electric/electronic controlled this time delay shall be reduced to maximum 0,2 s when the LHS control device is released.
Powered LHS movement after the operator returns to the normal operating position shall occur only when the LHS control device is activated from the neutral position.
This safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 3.
Where separate LHS controls remote from the normal operating position are provided, separate device for detecting the normal operating position can be overridden when the remote controls are selected.

Name: EN 1175 4.10.3 Insulation test (routine test) for high voltage trucks
EN 1175 4.9.2.5 Interlocking of guards
Note:
4.9.2.5 Interlocking of guards
If access gates/doors are provided with electrical interlocking, in accordance with EN ISO 3691- 3, this safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 6.

Name: EN 1175 B.7.2.3.2 Operating coils
EN 1175 B.7.1.1 General
Note:

Note:
4.5.1 General
For the drive system the following are considered as safe and can be used to achieve a safe state
e.g. in case of a failure in the drive system:
a) no driving torque, on the condition that the truck has an additional braking system which can be activated by the operator;
b) automatic braking by the drive system and/or by the braking system till and during standstill;
c) automatic speed reduction to a specific limit based on type, application and condition of the truck so long as the operator has full control and release of the speed control leads to the stopping of powered movement.
Failures of the electrical system leading to behaviour as mentioned in a), b) or c) or any combination thereof may be treated as a non-safety relevant failures.
NOTE 1 Control actions to achieve a safe state are only required for safety-related parts of control systems of Category 2 and higher as defined in EN ISO 13849-1.

NOTE 2 Additional information regarding the correspondence between requirements of 4.5 and most common causes of hazard can be found in Annex J.

NOTE 3 Experience shows that safe conditions designed in accordance with a) lead to an approximate braking effect which is 50 % of that achieved by options b) or c).

NOTE 4 Limitation in the use of a), b) and c) to achieve a safe state is indicated in the appropriate subclauses.

Name: EN 1175 4.1 Introduction
Note:
4.1 Introduction
Trucks shall comply with the safety requirements and/or protective measures of this clause. In addition, the truck shall be designed according to the principles of EN ISO 12100:2010 for relevant but not significant hazards which are not dealt with by this document.

Name: EN 1175 4.5.2 Travel control system
Note:
4.5.2 Travel control system
The travel control system shall be so arranged that on level ground the truck will start from standstill only when the control(s) for speed and direction are activated. For IC trucks, after engaging direction control, low speed is allowed without activation of the speed control.
Means shall be provided to avoid any truck movement when:
� switching on the travel control system;
� starting the engine of an IC truck.
Any initial activation of the drive system shall only be possible from the neutral position of the speed and/or directional control(s).
These safety functions shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 2.
NOTE Restart of the engine by a start/stop system is not considered as starting the engine.

Name: EN 1175 4.3.5.2 IC trucks
EN 1175 4.5.6.2 Uncontrolled acceleration from standstill on level ground
Note:
4.5.6.2 Uncontrolled acceleration from standstill on level ground
The drive system shall be so designed that uncontrolled hazardous acceleration from standstill on level ground is prevented.
This safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 2.
Any uncontrolled acceleration caused by an electrical failure is treated as hazardous when the criteria defined in Table 1 are exceeded.
Movement from rest in the wrong direction shall be considered hazardous.
NOTE Maximum truck acceleration at start is the maximum acceleration that the truck can perform from stationary when unladen.

Name: EN 1175 4.5.3 Monitoring of operating position
Note:
4.5.3 Monitoring of operating position
On sit-on rider-controlled trucks a separate device (OPC), independent of the speed control (accelerator), shall automatically bring an active drive system to a safe state, as defined in 4.5.1 a) or b) when the operator leaves the normal operating position.
On stand-on rider-controlled trucks a separate device (OPC), independent of the speed control (accelerator), shall automatically bring an active drive system to a safe state, as defined in 4.5.1 b) when the operator leaves the normal operating position.
Nuisance deactivation of the OPC due to operating conditions, such as rough ground, shall be prevented. The safe state shall be initiated not later than 2,0 s after deactivation of the OPC. This time delay shall be reduced to maximum 0,2 s when the speed control device is released. In addition to the deceleration provided by the OPC, the braking system shall be available to the operator.
Powered travel movement from standstill after the operator returns to the normal operating position shall occur only when the traction control device is activated from the neutral position.
During deceleration following release of the OPC while travelling, powered travel movement can be restored automatically provided that the speed control is active. Restoring the powered travel movement shall not cause hazardous accelerations which cannot be controlled by the operator.
Where separate travel controls other than those at the normal operating position are provided according to EN ISO 3691-1:2015, 4.4.2.6 the OPC can be overridden when this system is used. It shall not be possible to override the OPC when operation is from the normal operation position (e.g. interlock).
It shall be ensured that the resulting hazards when an additional control remote from the driving position is used are sufficiently reduced by additional measures, e.g. safe speed/acceleration limitation and/or personal detection means, where trucks are designed for travel controlled from outside and the detection device of operator position overridden.
These safety functions shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 2.

Name: EN 1175 4.4.2.1 Battery charging
Note:
4.4.2.1 Battery charging
When external charging supply cables are connected to the truck, truck movement shall be prevented. This safety function shall be in accordance with PLr as defined in Table 6. This does not apply to trucks designed only for permanent charging during operation.
The requirement is not intended for starter batteries.

Name: EN 1175 4.3.6 Protection from residual voltages
Note:
4.3.6 Protection from residual voltages
After disconnecting energy sources, the voltage of the capacitors in power circuits shall be less than 60 V DC after 10 s.
If the above condition is not technically achievable or practicable a warning/safety label shall be provided. This warning label shall be permanent and indelible and shall be affixed on, or in close proximity to, the enclosure containing the capacitors.
NOTE Safety signs EN ISO 7010 W001 and EN ISO 7010 W012 can be used.

Name: EN 1175 4.4.2.2 On board charger and/or additional components
Note:
4.4.2.2 On board charger and/or additional components
When trucks are fitted with on-board chargers or other devices connected to the mains, e.g. heaters, the requirements of EN 60204-1:2006, 6.3, 7.2.1 and Clause 8 up to and including 8.2 shall apply.
Enclosures containing equipment connected to the mains supply shall be in accordance with IPXXB of EN 60529:1991. However, for top surfaces the degree of protection shall be in accordance with at least IPXXD.
When the mains supply cables are connected to the truck it shall not be possible to induce any truck movement. This safety function shall be in accordance with PLr as defined in Table 6.
NOTE 1  Where a main external power supply socket could be switched off this requirement can be met by an interlock when the charger plug is in the home stowed position.

A position shall be provided on the truck to safely and properly store the cable, where permanently attached.
NOTE 2  The protective earth conductor of the on-board charger and additional components connected to the mains is essential for the protection against electrical shock in case of insulation fault.

Name: EN 1175 4.3.7 Overcurrent protection
Note:
4.3.7 Overcurrent protection
Power, control and auxiliary circuits shall be provided with overcurrent protection that is sized to prevent overheating of the smallest size conductor.
Overcurrent protective devices shall be capable of interrupting the maximum fault current without creating a fire hazard.
Overcurrent protective devices in the control and power circuits shall be as close as practicable to the energy source. Non-resettable overcurrent protective devices shall be identified according to the replacement rating of the device.
If the overcurrent protection is realized by electronic systems, e.g. by inverters or DC/DC converters, this function shall be in accordance with PLr as defined in Table 6.
Overcurrent protective devices shall be identified, and rating of these devices shall be indicated on the electrical diagram.
Replaceable overcurrent protective devices shall be provided with rating which shall be located on the truck, adjacent or close to the device itself.
NOTE For further information regarding location of overcurrent protective devices see EN 60204- 1:2006, 7.2.8 and EN 60204-1:2006, Annex D (informative).

Energy sources based on battery technology shall be equipped with a switching off device in accordance with 4.9.1.3. They shall be manually disconnectable and shall be automatically disconnected in case of an electrical fault related to the power system. They shall be provided with warning signs referring to high stored energy at high voltage. The warning signs shall be permanent and indelible.

Note:
C.2.4.4 Overtemperature
The BMS shall be designed such that corrective measures are initiated to prevent overtemperature exposure, e.g. deactivation of the battery. The limit of the overtemperature shall be specified by the manufacturer of the battery.
This safety related function shall have PLr = c in accordance with EN ISO 13849-1:2015.
NOTE Overtemperature arising from external heat sources cannot be prevented by the BMS.

Name: EN 1175 C.2.2.3
Note:
C.2.2.3
lithium-ion battery
system which incorporates one or more lithium-ion cells or battery packs, including a battery management system as well as disconnecting and/or isolating devices, e.g. contactors, disconnectors, fuses, etc. and mechanical elements
[SOURCE: EN 62620:2015, 3.10, modified]
Note 1 to entry:  lithium-ion batteries require protective circuits to work safely, see C.2.2.2.

Name: EN 1175 C.2.4.5 Undertemperature
Note:
C.2.4.5 Undertemperature
The BMS shall be designed such that corrective measures are initiated to prevent hazardous overcurrent while charging or discharging the battery if the temperature is below the critical limit specified by the manufacturer of the battery.
This safety related function shall have PLr = c in accordance with EN ISO 13849-1:2015.
NOTE Charging also means transferring energy to the battery from braking or other regenerative action.

Name: EN 1175 C.2.2.4
Note:
C.2.2.4
critical undervoltage limit
lowest discharge voltage of the battery cell below which the battery cannot be expected to be recoverable

Name: EN 1175 4.4.7 Electrical Components
Note:
4.4.7 Electrical Components
Conductors and cables shall conform to Annex G.

Name: EN 1175 G.1.1 General
Note:
G.1.1 General
Conductors and cables shall be selected to be suitable for the operating conditions and external influences that can exist, e.g. ambient temperature, presence of water or corrosive substances, mechanical stresses including during installation, fire hazards.
Conductors and cables shall be so placed and safeguarded as to avoid damage when the truck is in its normal operating condition as defined in EN ISO 3691-1:2015, 4.1.3.
The instructions given by the cable manufacturers about methods of installation, grouping and ambient temperature shall be applied.

Name: EN 1175 E.1 General
EN 1175 C.2.4.6 Overcurrent
Note:
C.2.4.6 Overcurrent
Overcurrent causing hazardous situations shall be prevented by fuses as part of the battery or equivalent measures initiated by the BMS.
The limit of the current shall be defined by the battery manufacturer.
This safety related function shall have PLr = c in accordance with EN ISO 13849-1:2015.

Name: EN 1175 C.2.2.5
Note:
C.2.2.5
recuperation
electric power generated by the truck electric systems recharging the battery

Name: EN 1175 G.1.2 Protection
Note:
G.1.2 Protection
Power circuit conductors and cables shall be flame retardant, self-extinguishing and at least in compliance with EN 50565-1.
Flame propagation characteristic of cables shall be tested in accordance with EN 60332-1-2 with at least the results recommended in Annex A or in accordance with EN 60695-11-10, at least grade V-2.
Other plastic means of protection of conductors (for instance, conduits) shall be classified at least HB in accordance with EN 60695-11-10.
Wiring and electrical components shall be designed, placed or protected to minimize contamination and fire hazards arising from operating fluids (such as fuel or oil) leakage.
NOTE Additional guidance for the correct selection and use of cables can be found in the EN 50525 series of standards.

Name: EN 1175 C.2.2 Terms and definitions
Note:
C.2.2 Terms and definitions
For the purposes of this annex, the terms and definitions given in ISO 5053-1 and the following apply.

Name: EN 1175 G.1.4.2 Identification
Note:
G.1.4.2 Identification
Wires, cables, and terminals shall be identified by coding which shall be consistent with the electrical diagram included in the service manual.
When the electrical connections are made through plug-socket connectors, there shall be measures to minimize any incorrect connection between them other than that intended, if this can cause hazard.
In the same plug/socket connector there shall not be two or more wires with the same identification which correspond at different signals.

Name: EN 1175 E.3 Information for use
Note:
E.3 Information for use
Assistance systems shall conform to Clause 6.
The instruction manual shall include the scope, the safety instructions, the limits, the use and the other relevant characteristics of the assistance systems to allow the training of the industrial truck operator and the correct use. It shall be stated that the operator shall be cautioned against developing dependence on assistance systems, thus disregarding normal conservative behaviours.
Training of the operator shall also include the correct and safe use of the truck in case of sudden failure of the assistance system.

Name: EN 1175 C.2.6.2 Type plate
EN 1175 C.2.4.1 General
Note:
C.2.4.1 General
Batteries and battery cells shall meet the requirements of EN 62619. The following clauses define additional requirements specific for industrial trucks.
All battery safety functions shall be ensured by the BMS. This requirement shall be fulfilled in all operating situations including charging and storage, e.g. replacement batteries.

Name: EN 1175 C.2.2.3
Note:
C.2.2.3
lithium-ion cell
secondary single cell whose electrical energy is derived from the insertion/extraction reactions of lithium ions between the anode and the cathode
[SOURCE: ISO 18300:2016, 3.10]

Name: EN 1175 C.2.2.2
Note:
C.2.2.2
BMS
battery management system
electronic system associated with a battery which monitors and/or manages its state, calculates secondary data, reports that data and/or controls its environment to influence the battery�s safety, performance and/or service life and has the functions to cut off in case of overcharging, overcurrent and overheating
[SOURCE: EN 62620:2015, 3.11]
Note 1 to entry:  The function of the BMS can be assigned to the battery pack or to equipment that uses the battery.

Name: EN 1175 G.1.4.1 General
Note:
G.1.4.1 General
All connections, especially those of the protective bonding circuit, shall be secured against accidental loosening.
The means of connection shall be suitable for the cross-sectional areas and nature of the conductors being terminated.
The terminations of cables shall be adequately supported to limit mechanical stresses at the terminations of the conductors.
Where unintended or accidental disconnection of plug/socket combinations can cause a hazardous situation, they shall have a retaining means.
Connections to frequently moving parts shall be made using conductors in accordance with EN 60204-1:2006, 12.6.1 and 12.6.2.
Cables subject to movement shall be supported in such a way that there is no excessive mechanical strain on the connection points nor any sharp flexing.
Where flexible conduit is adjacent to moving parts, the construction and supporting means shall prevent damage to the flexible conduit under all conditions of operation.

Name: EN 1175 E.2.3 Reliability
EN 1175 C.2.6.1 Signals
Note:
C.2.6.1 Signals
Warning signals (audible and/or visual) shall be provided before the BMS shuts down the lithium- ion battery due to a low state of charge.
Displays showing the state of charge are suitable as a signal.
Displays and visual warning signals shall be located in a way that the truck operator has a plain view from the normal operator�s position.

Name: EN 1175 C.2.6.3 Instruction handbook
EN 1175 C.2.4.2 Overvoltage
Note:
C.2.4.2 Overvoltage
The BMS shall be designed such that voltage exceeding the highest voltage in the operating region from a safety standpoint does not cause hazardous related situations. The limit of the overvoltage shall be specified by the manufacturer of the battery.
This safety related function shall have PLr = c in accordance with EN ISO 13849-1:2015.

Name: EN 1175 C.2.2.1
Note:
C.2.2.1
lithium-ion battery pack
one or more lithium-ion cells electrically connected and mechanical elements e.g. trays, mounting material

Name: EN 1175 D.3.1.2 Insulation test
Note:
D.3.1.2 Insulation test
The electric drive system shall conform to the requirements of 4.10.

Name: EN 1175 C.2.4.3 Undervoltage
Note:
C.2.4.3 Undervoltage
If one of the battery cells is discharged below the critical undervoltage limit, the BMS shall not permit charging the battery again.
This safety related function shall have PLr = c in accordance with EN ISO 13849-1:2015.
NOTE The BMS is usually designed to avoid a further discharge operation before the battery is discharged below the critical undervoltage limit specified by the manufacturer of the battery.

Name: EN 1175 D.2.4 Type plates
Note:
D.2.4 Type plates
The components of electric drive systems shall be provided with indelible and not easily detachable type plates. Type plates of motors and converters shall include information ensuring traceability e.g. a serial number.
To inhibit unexpected or uncontrollable movements of the electric drive system the terminal marking shall ensure for example the right connection of the wiring with the components or the correct exchange with spare parts. Terminal marking shall be in accordance with EN 60034-8.
Components of the electric drive system with nominal voltages of the energy source greater than 96 V or equipped with a high-power energy source (e.g. electric double layer capacitors) shall be marked with a durable hazard or warning labels.

Name: EN 1175 C.2.3.2 Environmental conditions of the BMS
Note:
C.2.3.2 Environmental conditions of the BMS
The BMS shall be designed and built to withstand the following tests, without malfunctioning or loosening of parts:
a) Vibration
Test in accordance with EN 60068-2-6: sinusoidal amplitude from 10 Hz to 500 Hz, change rate of frequency 1 octave/min, with acceleration 30 m/s2, 3 axes with duration of 2 h per axis.
b) Shock
Test in accordance with EN 60068-2-27: half-sinusoidal amplitude with minimum acceleration 400 m/s2 for 6 ms, 3 000 times in each of 6 axes (x, y, and z, both directions).
After execution of the tests, the requirements of C.2.4 shall be verified.

Name: EN 1175 F.4 Assisted steering systems
Note:
F.4 Assisted steering systems
The steering wheel is directly coupled with the steering axle by a mechanical/hydraulic system. The hydrostatic steering valve includes an oil pump driven by the steering wheel, which guarantees the steering function even though the hydraulic oil supply (1) fails. An electrical failure of the oil supply system cannot lead to an unintended steering. Shown in Figure F.4.

Name: EN 1175 D.3.1.1 Overspeed test
Note:
D.3.1.1 Overspeed test
The motor and generator if applicable shall be designed to withstand an overspeed test.
An overspeed test at 1,2 times the maximum design rotational frequency of the motor shall be carried out for a minimum duration of 2 min. An overspeed test shall be considered as satisfactory if no permanent deformation is apparent.

Name: EN 1175 F.3.2 Electric powered assistance
Note:
F.3.2 Electric powered assistance
The steering wheel and the electrical powered assistance system both influence the steering angle in parallel, either directly coupled or through a differential gear. By using a differential gear independent operation by the steering wheel and the assistance system is possible. This kind of system is shown in Figure F.2.
The steering system depicted in Figure F.2 a) can also belong to the type described in F.4 if a limited power/torque of the motor allows the operator to control the steering in case of electric failure.

Name: EN 1175 E.2.1 Control by the operator
Note:
E.2.1 Control by the operator
The design of assistance systems shall always allow the operator to bring the truck to a safe state.

Name: EN 1175 D.2.3 Maximum rotational speed
Note:
D.2.3 Maximum rotational speed
The maximum rotational speed shall be defined by the truck manufacturer regarding type and operation of the truck.

Name: EN 1175 C.2.5 Electromagnetic radiation
Note:
C.2.5 Electromagnetic radiation
The requirements of 4.3.10 apply to BMSs, which shall be tested either as part of a complete truck or separately in a system test.

Name: EN 1175 C.2.3.1 Mechanical requirements
Note:
C.2.3.1 Mechanical requirements
Lithium-ion batteries shall be designed and tested at least in accordance to the requirements of EN 62281 and EN 62619. In addition, specific mechanical stress that can occur in industrial trucks shall be considered.
If the truck manufacturer provides a specification with more stringent requirements, the battery shall be verified for these conditions.
After execution of the required tests all safety requirements shall be maintained.
To avoid damage during transport and assembling/disassembling, the battery shall be equipped with lifting and/or slinging points. These points shall be indicated on the battery.
NOTE 1   Vibration and shock are specific to the design and the use of the truck.

NOTE 2  It is possible to transfer measurement results to batteries of the same design but different sizes if a representative battery design is used.

Name: EN 1175 Figure F.2 - Electrically powered backup
EN 1175 E.2.2 System design
Note:
E.2.2 System design
Assistance systems shall not impair the safe operability of the truck. If assistance systems increase the level of risk or generate new risks, appropriate safety measures shall be applied (see for instance 4.5.5 or 4.6.6).

Name: EN 1175 4.9.1.3 Switching off device
Note:
4.9.1.3 Switching off device
The switching off device shall be capable of interrupting the normal maximum current by one of the following methods:
a) for nominal voltages not greater than 96 V a connector specified in Annex A, Range 1; 9
b) manually actuated power switch directly disconnecting one line of power circuit;
c) manually actuated control switch disconnecting the power supply to the coil of one contactor in one line of the power supply and disconnecting or disabling the electronic power switching circuit, e.g. inverter or controller for AC motors. In trucks driven by series-wound DC motors with mechanical commutator, two independent contactors are required to switch off the battery supply;
d) manually actuated control switch disconnecting one line of the power supply by a solid-state switch. This technical solution shall be applicable only for trucks with main drive system designed with AC technology.
When methods b), c) or d) are used, switching off devices shall be of positive action type complying with EN 60947-5-5 and the control coloured red.
When method c) is used, electromagnetic contactors shall be in conformance with Annex B.
It shall be possible to re-establish the supply to the power transmission systems only by manual resetting of the switching off control followed by the normal operation of the controls.
For IC trucks the device that activates/deactivates the main electrical system, e.g. the ignition switch, may be used as the switching off device if it deactivates truck movements.

Name: EN 1175 4.5.11 Interface for speed limitation
Note:
4.5.11 Interface for speed limitation
If trucks are provided with interfaces for external speed limitation, changes of speed caused by the external system shall be limited by the truck logic to a level that can be controlled by the operator (for instance see 4.5.5, 4.5.7).
The external speed limitation shall not exceed the limit set by the truck controller.
NOTE Systems for speed limitation installed by the person responsible for the operation of a truck, giving the maximum speed setpoint to the truck control unit via an electrical interface are outside the scope of this document. Suitable requirements consistent with this document, can be determined by risk assessment by the responsible person.

Name: EN 1175 G.1.3 Cross-sectional area
Note:
G.1.3 Cross-sectional area
The cross-sectional area shall be so selected that during normal operation of the truck the temperature does not exceed the temperature rating of insulation used.
Copper conductors external to enclosures (excluding short connections between electric or electronic components and wires that are an integral part of a proprietary component) shall ensure adequate mechanical strength.
NOTE To achieve the above requirements the manufacturer can apply EN 60204-1:2006, 12.2 and 12.4.

Name: EN 1175 4.5.10 Speed limitation
EN 1175 4.10.4 Frame fault test
Note:
4.10.4 Frame fault test
The frame fault test simulates a frame fault at each electric motor which is fed by a pulse control,
e.g. by a converter. Low power motors, for example wiper or fan motors, are excluded from this test.
When introducing the frame fault the motor shall be set to a minimum of 20 % of the maximum operational speed for duration of 5 s. Inadvertent movement shall not occur.
During the test of the drive system the truck shall be jacked up (idled drive wheels).

Name: EN 1175 4.10.1 Dielectric test (type test)
Note:
4.10.1 Dielectric test (type test)
The dielectric test shall be performed to battery driven trucks with traction battery disconnected and to IC trucks equipped with electric power transmission systems.
Trucks shall be designed to conform to a type test performed on a new, dry truck using an AC or DC test voltage in accordance with Table 5. The test voltage shall be supplied from a power source with a minimum rating of 500 VA.
Test voltage shall be the applied between truck frame and each active part of the power circuits. The elements of these active parts may be tested in common, if they are connected with low impedance e.g. by the free-wheeling diodes of a converter or the motor windings.
If control circuits and low power auxiliary circuits10 can be damaged by the test voltage, they may be excluded from the test, i.e. disconnected or bypassed.
The test voltage shall be applied for 1 min. During this time no dielectric breakdown shall occur.

Name: EN 1175 4.6.2 Movement from standstill
Note:
4.6.2 Movement from standstill
Movement of a function of the LHS from standstill shall be possible only by operating the dedicated control for an LHS function, e.g. joysticks.
Means shall be provided to avoid any movement of a function of the LHS:
� while switching on the system;
� while starting the engine of an IC truck.
After switching on the LHS control system and/or after starting the engine, initial activation of the LHS shall only be possible from the neutral position of the controls intended for LHS.
This safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 3.
NOTE 1 Restart of the engine by a start/stop system is not considered as starting the engine.

NOTE 2 Movement of LHS functions caused by a non-electric fault is not part of this safety requirement,
e.g. creeping of lifting system caused by leakage of hydraulic valves.

Name: EN 1175 4.5.8 Electrically/electronic controlled service brake
Note:
4.5.8 Electrically/electronic controlled service brake
Electrical and electronic control systems of the service brake shall be designed to ensure the required brake function operates correctly or fail safe.
The design shall ensure that an electrical failure will not increase the risk of brake failure e.g. because of friction caused by a permanently partly released brake. This safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 2.
NOTE Examples of supervision of the correct functioning of a non-inherently safe mechanical brake are the monitoring of the braking pressure, the position of the brake cylinder or the current of the braking coil.

Name: EN 1175 4.9.1.2.2
Note:
4.9.1.2.2 For electrically powered trucks, the actuation of the switching off control shall initiate the interruption of the electrical power supplies to all power circuits:
� within 0,2 s for stop category 0;
� within 5 s for stop category 1.
This safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 6.
If the switching off function of electrically powered trucks is realized by an electric/electronic control system, it shall be independent from other potentially hazardous systems.
NOTE �independent� means that any other truck control system cannot disable the switching off function. Category 3 control systems according to EN ISO 13849-1:2015 are an example that achieves independency.

Name: EN 1175 Table 3 - Performance levels of LHS system
EN 1175 4.5.6.3 Unintended truck behaviour while truck is moving
Note:
4.5.6.3 Unintended truck behaviour while truck is moving
The drive system shall be so designed that unintended hazardous truck behaviour while truck is moving is prevented. This safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 2.
The following behaviour caused by an electrical failure is considered hazardous:
a) no reaction of reverse or neutral travel direction when demanded by the operator;
b) acceleration unrelated to the operator input and uncontrollable by operator adjustment of speed control (accelerator) during travel operation on level ground that:
� is higher than 30 % of the maximum acceleration achievable by the truck under no fault condition
and/or
� which results in a speed that exceeds the operator requested speed setpoint by more than 20 % of maximum speed achievable by the truck under no fault condition.
NOTE List item a) is only relevant for trucks with separate direction selector.

Name: EN 1175 6.7 Non-ionising radiation
Note:
6.7 Non-ionising radiation
Warning shall be given in the instruction manual if after the commissioning the truck can be equipped with devices that are likely to emit non-ionising radiation which can cause harm to persons, in particular those with active or non-active implantable medical devices, e.g. radio- transmitters, RFID readers or data collection systems.
Where trucks are fitted with non-ionising radiation devices which can cause harm to persons, warning signs shall be installed.

Name: EN 1175 4.6.1 General
Note:
4.6.1 General
A stationary LHS is considered as a safe state.
NOTE 1 The stationary condition can be achieved by taking the LHS to one or more of the following states, as applicable considering the type of truck and the technology used:

a) electric motor which powers the load handling system directly, switched off;

b) oil supply system deactivated;

c) electrical actuated valves switched off, where the hydraulic system is possibly kept under pressure.

Even when the LHS is controlled by manually operated valves, the requirements regarding LHS safety functions realized by an electric/electronic system shall be fulfilled.
NOTE 2 Additional information regarding the correspondence between requirements of 4.6 and most common causes of hazard can be found in Annex J.

Name: EN 1175 4.5.7 Unintended deceleration
Note:
4.5.7 Unintended deceleration
Under normal operating conditions as defined in EN ISO 3691-1:2015, 4.1.3, unintended deceleration caused by an electric/electronic failure of the electronic controlled service brake, parking brake or the drive system shall not lead to tip-over. Inherently safe design of electronic controlled service brake shall be considered as satisfying this requirement.
This safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 2.

Name: EN 1175 6.8 Interoperability of energy sources
Note:
6.8 Interoperability of energy sources
Detailed information shall be provided concerning the interoperability of the truck with different battery technologies and with batteries of different rating of current and voltage, if applicable.

Name: EN 1175 4.5.9.3 Indication of parking brake state
Note:
4.5.9.3 Indication of parking brake state
Automatically or manually applied parking brake state shall be indicated to the operator when engaged. The exceptions to this requirement are brake systems fitted to stand-on and pedestrian controlled trucks equipped with a brake system that will automatically engage upon release of the brake actuating control in accordance with EN ISO 3691-1:2015, 4.3.3.
An electrical indication of the parking brake state is not required when power supply of the truck has been switched off (see EN ISO 3691-1:2015, 4.2.2.1).
This safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 2.

Name: EN 1175 6.6.1 General
Note:
6.6.1 General
Electrical enclosures for trucks with nominal voltages greater than of 120 V shall bear a durable warning sign conforming to EN 60204-1:2006, 16.2.

Name: EN 1175 5.3.3 Bonding
Note:
5.3.3 Bonding
Equipotential bonding shall be provided between the frame of the vehicle and metallic electrical enclosures e.g. motor frames. The equipotential bonding shall ensure the same electric potential under all conditions which can be caused by the electrical system of the truck.
The status of the equipotential bonding shall be part of the routine test.

Name: EN 1175 Table 2 - Performance levels of drive system
EN 1175 Table 1 - Limits for acceptable uncontrolled acceleration/movements
EN 1175 6.6.2 Electronic controller
EN 1175 4.5.9.1 Trucks with automatic parking brake
Note:
4.5.9.1 Trucks with automatic parking brake
a) Automatic operation of parking brakes shall not result in hazardous situations. The control system of the parking brake shall be designed to prevent the automatic release of the parking brake not intended by the operator.
Where activating the travel control device can result in automatic release of the parking brake, it shall not result in hazardous truck movements which cannot be controlled by the operator.
These safety functions shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 2.
b) With the truck at standstill, the parking brake shall be applied if the operator is not in the normal operating position.
This safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 2.
c) When the truck is designed to hold the truck on a ramp stationary or at low speed by the drive system and the travel control is released, the parking brake shall be activated automatically before the drive system loses the ability to hold the truck.
This safety function shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 2.
d) Failure of the control system of an automatically applied parking brake shall be indicated to the operator (see EN ISO 3691-1:2015, 4.2.2.1).
The safety function of failure detection shall be in accordance with PLr as defined in Table 2.

Name: EN 1175 6.3 Electrical interface for external systems
Note:
6.3 Electrical interface for external systems
The interface specification for the external system shall be included in the truck instruction handbook. If applicable, the achievable performance level of the functions provided by the interface shall be specified in the instructions.
Warning shall be given in the service manual that field modification and installation of electrical accessories shall be carried out and documented by trained personal only, and the requirements of this document shall be maintained.

Name: EN 1175 5.2.4 Emergency disconnection
Note:
5.2.4 Emergency disconnection
Provision shall be made to prevent the use of battery connectors for emergency disconnection purposes.

Name: EN 1175 4.5.9.2 Trucks without automatically applied parking brake
Note:
4.5.9.2 Trucks without automatically applied parking brake
If the movement of a truck without an automatically applied parking brake is actively controlled or minimized by the drive system, measures shall be taken so that the operator becomes aware of this situation, e.g. creeping of the truck on a ramp at low speed.
Measures shall be taken to warn the operator before leaving the truck (see EN ISO 3691-1:2015, 4.2.2.1) without applying the brake as long as the power supply of the truck is not switched off by the operator.
If the required warning is realized by an electric/electronic system, it shall be in accordance with the PLr as defined in Table 2.

Name: EN 1175 6.4 Safety checks
Note:
6.4 Safety checks
Methods and intervals for checking safety systems shall be included in the service manual and/or instruction handbook.

Name: EN 1175 A.4.6.3 Test of disconnection under emergency conditions for Range 1 only
Note:
A.4.6.3 Test of disconnection under emergency conditions for Range 1 only
Each assembly of two coupled half-connectors shall be connected to a source of direct current through an inductive circuit having an impedance such that the time constant of the circuit is 15 ms and the current to be broken shall be 3 times the rated current, when connected to a supply voltage of 96 V.
The connector shall be capable of clearing any arc which is drawn because of this emergency disconnection. It is not imperative that the two halves of the connector should remain serviceable after this test.

Name: EN 1175 A.4.1 General
Note:
A.4.1 General
Testing shall be carried out following the sequence outlined in Figure A.1. Failing of a single test shall result in rejection of the component.

Name: EN 1175 A.3.5 Reversal-polarity protection
Note:
A.3.5 Reversal-polarity protection
To prevent reversal of polarity the casings shall have incorporated a non-removable mechanical device ensuring the non-reversibility of polarity of the two half-connectors.
Contacts and other current-carrying parts when connected or separated shall not come into contact with metallic parts of the connector casing.

Name: EN 1175 6.1 General
Note:
6.1 General
The following requirements shall apply in addition to those of the applicable industrial trucks� safety standards of EN ISO 3691 series and EN 16307 series.

Name: EN 1175 5.2.2 Charger switching
Note:
5.2.2 Charger switching
For batteries with an end-of-charge voltage exceeding 120 V, switching of external chargers shall be controlled via the connector auxiliary contacts or other devices to prevent arcing at the connector and to ensure that the charger is not energised until it is connected to the battery.
NOTE The end-of-charge voltage of a 96 V lead acid battery is below 120 V.

Name: EN 1175 6.2 Electrical diagram
Note:
6.2 Electrical diagram
Circuit diagrams shall comply with EN 60204-1:2006, Clause 17. If the truck is provided with power outlets or connection points/ports for auxiliary lighting, on-board computers, assistance systems etc. the instruction handbook shall give clear indication of location, usage, interface specifications and scope.

Name: EN 1175 5.2.3 Requirements
Note:
5.2.3 Requirements
Connectors shall conform to Annex A, Range 2.

Name: EN 1175 B.7.2.4 Dielectric test
EN 1175 B.7.1.3 Routine tests
Note:
B.7.1.3 Routine tests
Routine tests are intended to detect faults in materials and workmanship and to ascertain proper functioning of the equipment. They shall be made on each individual piece of equipment.
Routine tests shall at least comprise:
� functional test (operating limit);
� dielectric test or insulation resistance test.

Name: EN 1175 B.5.1 Normal service conditions
Note:
B.5.1 Normal service conditions
Contactors conforming to this annex shall be capable of operating under following standard conditions:
� Climatic conditions as described in the scope of this document.
� Pollution degree: contactors shall be designed for use in pollution degree 3 environments.
NOTE Environment is said to be pollution degree 3 when conductive pollution occurs, or dry, non- conductive pollution occurs which becomes conductive due to condensation. See EN 60664-1:2007, 4.6.2.

Name: EN 1175 B.3.3 Type B
Note:
B.3.3 Type B
NC (normally closed) in which the main contacts are close when the operating coil is not energised. The contacts shall be capable of making, carrying and breaking the current of the main circuit.

Name: EN 1175 B.5.2 Mounting
Note:
B.5.2 Mounting
Contactors shall be mounted in accordance with the manufacturer instructions.

Name: EN 1175 B.3.4 Type C
Note:
B.3.4 Type C
CO (change-over) in which there are two sets of main contacts: one set NO and one set NC, with or without a common point. The NO contacts shall be capable of making, carrying and breaking currents. The NC contacts shall not be required to break current but shall be capable of carrying rated thermal current.

Name: EN 1175 B.2.1
Note:
B.2.1
Ith
conventional free air thermal current
maximum test current fulfilling the requirements of the temperature-rise test of the unenclosed equipment in free air
Note 1 to entry: The value of the conventional free air thermal current shall be at least equal to the maximum value of the rated operational current (see B.2.2) of the unenclosed equipment.

Note 2 to entry: Free air is understood to be in air under normal indoor conditions reasonably free from draughts and external radiation.

Name: EN 1175 A.4.7 Testing the other 2 of 4 connectors
EN 1175 C.1.4 Battery with nominal voltage exceeding 96 V DC
EN 1175 B.7.2.9.1 Verification of vibration
EN 1175 A.4.6.1 Low temperature test
Note:
A.4.6.1 Low temperature test
Maintain connectors at a temperature of (?20 � 1) �C for 16 h. Name: EN 1175 1 Scope

1 Scope
This document specifies the electrical requirements for the design and construction of the electrical installation in self-propelled industrial trucks that are within the scope of ISO 5053-1, except variable reach trucks as defined in ISO 5053-1:2015, 3.21 and 3.22, straddle carriers as defined in ISO 5053-1:2015, 3.18 and 3.19, and specific functions, parts and/or systems utilized for the automatic operation of driverless industrial trucks as defined in ISO 5053-1:2015, 3.32. It provides the electrical/electronic and safety-related parts of control system requirements for those self-propelled industrial trucks identified above to complete the requirements in the relevant part of the EN ISO 3691 and EN 16307 series of documents.
NOTE 1 Reference is made to this document in other standards which cover the non-electrical requirements of the various industrial truck types.

The requirements of this document are valid when trucks are operated under the following climatic conditions:
� defined in the applicable parts of the EN ISO 3691 series and the EN 16307 series;
� relative humidity in the range 30 % to 95 % (not condensing).
This document deals with safety requirements for all electrical and electronic components of industrial trucks, including electrically actuated hydraulic/pneumatic valves. It specifies minimum performance levels required for safety functions realized by safety related parts of control systems. It is intended to be used to avoid or minimize hazards or hazardous situations listed in Annex I. These situations can arise during the operation in the area of use for which it is designed and during maintenance of trucks in accordance with the specifications and instruction given by the manufacturer.
This document does not deal with hazards which could occur:
a) during construction;
b) when operating in potentially explosive atmospheres;
c) because of malfunction of non-electric safety-related parts of control systems, e.g. hydraulic and pneumatic elements like pistons, non-electric valves, pumps etc.
NOTE 2  The level of the defined required performance for electrical safety related control systems can be used as a guideline to determine the performance of non-electric systems.

NOTE 3 Hazards due to penetration of water and dust are covered by the definition of PLr of safety functions, according to EN ISO 13849-1:2015.

Name: 3.5.6 Legacy Commands
Note:
In previous versions of GSE software, certain commands were allowed on the diagnostic port which did not require a sync or termination character. Name: 3.5.2 Commands
Note:
Commands will be designated by a command string. All commands begin with '!' followed by a lower case letter command code and end with <CR>, where <CR> is a placeholder for the terminating carriage return and optional line feed. Command codes with no arguments can be any length up to the max message length. Commands with arguments must have a command code that is exactly 3 characters long. If a command contains multiple arguments, the arguments will be separated with commas(,). The total length of the command must not exceed the maximum message length (see Memory Requirements).
The following commands are available:
[TABLE]

Name: 3.5.3 Data Requests
Note:
Data Requests are commands which expect information to be returned by the charger. All data requests are responded to by sending an echo of the request followed by the requested data item. If the data item is not available, the response will just be the echoed request with an empty data field.
All data requests begin with '?' or"!?" followed by a lower case letter data type code of 3 characters, and end with <CR>, where <CR> is a placeholder for the terminating carriage return and optional line feed. If the data item is associated with a port, the port ID will precede the data request code. If the port was not explicitly specified in the request, the data will be sent for the first port (port A).
The following data request commands are available. Port related data items are shown with port A's format. For port B, replace ?pidA with ?pidB. For single port chargers, the port specifier is optional and returned data items will not be preceded by a port identifier.
[TABLE]

Name: 3.5.4 Multiple Data Item Requests
Note:
Multiple data items can be requested in a single message with no <CR> separator to save bandwidth. The selected data items are listed in sequence using the same format as specified in the previous section. The '?' character is used as a field separator. The port ID field sets the port for all following fields. The entire message is terminated with the <CR> sequence.
Example: I want to request the battery ID, battery type, and amp-hr capacity of the vehicle currently connected to port B.
Send !?pidB?bid?btp?bcp<CR>
Receive !?pidB?bidBAT05?btp43?bcp500<CR>
Note that although the fields in this example are sent back in the same order as they were requested, this is not a hard requirement. Fields may be sent in any order. Fields which are not available will be returned with an empty data portion.

Name: 3.5.5 Defined Data Set Requests
Note:
Certain predefined data sets are given unique 3 letter packet identifiers because they either group together related items or they all petain to a specific event. The table below lists the expected data items to be returned by these packet requests. If no data is available for an item, it will be returned as a 3 -letter field code with no data following. For example, certain items are only available when vehicle is connected, or when a charge is in progress, etc.
Port related data items are shown with port A's format. For port B, replace ?pidA with ?pidB. For single port chargers the port identifier is optional and returned items will not be preceded by it.

Name: 3.2 Timing Requirements
Note:
Not all commands require a response. If a response is expected, the entire response must be returned within 20 ms of the last received byte of the command. If the response times out the client should assume a failure to respond.
If the communication channel is synchronous, the client will need to wait for a response or timeout before sending the next command. However, if the channel is asynchronous, the client does not need to wait for a response before sending the next command.
The MVS does not have a timeout requirement. Typed characters will remain in the receive buff er until one of the following occurs:
1) A terminator is received (e.g. <CR>) - process command
2) The maximum number of characters is received - process command
3) A new command sync character is received('!') - buffer is cleared and wait for new command
4) The charger firmware is reset or loses power - command data is lost

Name: 3.3 Memory Requirements
Note: The maximum length of client command to the charger will be 128 bytes (this requirement does not apply to OTA download data). The maximum length of a response message will be 256 bytes.

Name: 3.4 Transport Layer
Note: All messages between the client and the charger will begin with a '!' character or '?' character and end with a terminator which is a carriage return (0x0D), plus an optional line feed (0x0A). The terminator will be designated <CR> from here on. If a '!' or '?' is received, the system will buffer characters until <CR> is received or the max number of characters is received (see Memory Requirements), after which the message is processed and the system waits for the next message. However, if another'!' character is received before the initial message is complete, the interrupted message is ignored, the input buffer is cleared, and the new message takes precedence. Thus, it is important that message data does not contain the characters '! ', 0x0D, or 0x0A.

Name: 3.5 Command Layer
Note:
Commands beginning with'!' will be executed but not be responded to. Commands beginning with '?' or'!?' are considered queries and will require a response. Note that the '!' in front of a query is optional, but using provides a better chance of clear reception. See Timing Requirements for response times. If a command is not correctly formatted, it will be ignored.
Format Specifiers
Data items for read or write commands are specified in standard ascii formats. These formats will be specified using symbols which are explained here:

This designator is optional if a charger has only one port. The port ID specifier precedes the data without a <CR> termination after it. See next sections for examples.

Name: Offline data loss

#7: Data recovery 
5/5 for customer problems

Problem statement: When testing the data recovery feature of the skylink kit, it seemed like the kits did not send any of the data that it had collected while the unit was offline. Expected behavior is that when the Skylink kit goes offline, the charger should still be collecting and logging the data of any charging sessions that occur. When the skylink kit returns to online status, it should grab data from the charger to capture all the charging sessions that occurred while the kit was offline, and then it should subsequently send that data to the cloud backend (Skylink) to ensure no data is lost and all data is recorded + reported. This does not currently happen. When a skylink kit goes offline and comes back online, no data is retroactively recorded in the Skylink system. This is a huge problem as it means that we’re actively losing data every time our Skylink kits go offline, even intermittently, which is something that we know happens often based on reports from the field. 
Data recovery fails when Skylink kit goes offline.
Customers lose critical charging session data, compromising compliance with reporting regulations and operational insights. Data integrity is essential for customers, especially for regulatory reporting and audits. Missing data may result in fines or loss of funding.
