Note: Metal-to-metal hinge bearing members may be considered as a means for bonding the door for grounding.

Name: UL 1564 26.10
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
On a permanently connected or cord-connected product, the size of a conductor or a strap employed to bond an electrical enclosure or motor frame shall be based on the rating of the branch-circuit overcurrent device to which the product will be connected. The size of the conductor or strap shall be in accordance with Table 26.1.
Exception: A smaller conductor or strap may be used if it complies with the Grounding Impedance Test,Section 37.

Name: UL 1564 26.9
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A connection that depends upon the clamping action exerted by rubber or similar material may be acceptable if it complies with Section 44, Bonding Conductor Test, for bonding conductors under any normal degree of compression permitted by a variable clamping device and if the results are still acceptable after exposure to the effects of oil, grease, moisture, and thermal degradation that are likely too ccur in service. Also, the effect of assembling and disassembling, for maintenance purposes, such a clamping device is to be considered with particular emphasis on the likelihood of it being reassembled in its intended position.

Name: UL 1564 26.6
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A single-point reference ground may be employed in a low-voltage or isolated-limited-secondary circuit. The enclosure, frame, or panel, including bolted joints, may carry the current of a low-voltage circuit. In neither of these instances is such current to be carried through the field-equipment grounding means, the metallic raceway or other power-supply grounding means, or the earth ground. See 24.4.1.

Name: UL 1564 26.5
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: Other than as noted in 26.6, the circuitry shall be arranged so that the equipment-grounding connection or conductor, the enclosure, the frame, the component mounting panel, and the earth ground do not carry current except during an electrical fault.

Name: UL 1564 26.8
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The bonding shall be by a positive means, such as by clamps, rivets, bolted, or screwed connections, or by welding, soldering, or brazing with materials having a softening or melting point greater than 455�C (850�F). The bonding connection shall penetrate nonconductive coatings, such as paint or vitreous enamel. Bonding around a resilient mount shall not depend on the clamping action of rubber or similar material, other than as indicated in 26.9.

Name: UL 1564 32.2.3
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: An oven may be used to condition the samples to the temperature attained under the conditions specified in 32.2.1 and 32.2.2 before conducting the test described in those paragraphs.

Name: UL 1564 SA3.2
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The enclosure of an outdoor unit shall be protected against outdoor exposure in accordance with the requirements in SA3.3 � SA3.15.

Name: UL 1564 SA3.3
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: Metal shall not be used in combination such as to cause galvanic action that adversely affects an enclosure.

Name: UL 1564 49.8
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: In accordance with the Exception to 20.2, a product not provided with input-circuit overcurrent protection shall be marked with the word �CAUTION � and the following or the equivalent: �Risk of Fire. Use only on circuits provided with _____ amperes branch circuit protection in accordance with the National Electrical Code, NFPA 70.� The marking shall be provided: a) On the product in a visible location; or b) In the operating manual provided with the product.

Name: UL 1564 49.9
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: If an abnormal operation or a transformer burnout test, or both, is concluded by operation of branch-circuit overcurrent protection as mentioned in 39.1.5 and 40.1.3, the marking specified in 49.8 shall be provided.

Name: UL 1564 SA3.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: As an alternative to the requirements in SA3 � SA9, enclosures shall comply with requirements for enclosures intended for outdoor exposure in the Standard for Enclosures for Electrical Equipment, UL 50.

Name: UL 1564 16.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
A fan motor used in a product shall be provided with protection consisting of one of the following:
a) Thermal or impedance protection complying with the requirements in the Standard for Overheating Protection for Motors, UL 2111, or the Standard for Impedance Protected Motors, UL 1004-2, or the Standard for Thermally Protected Motors, UL 1004-3; or
b) Other protection that is shown by testing to be equivalent to the protection mentioned in (a).
Exception: A fan motor with the air-propelling component coupled directly to the motor shaft complying with the requirements in 6.15(b) and with 39.4.1 need not have the protection indicated in (a) or (b).
UL 2111 to be withdrawn on September 15, 2014

Name: UL 1564 32.1.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
32.1.1 A product shall withstand for 1 minute without breakdown the application of a 40 to 70 hertz essentially sinusoidal potential with the product at the maximum operating temperature:
a) One thousand volts plus twice the maximum rated voltage between:
1) The primary circuit and dead metal parts;
2) The primary and secondary circuits; and
3) All secondary windings, including any ferro-resonant windings.
b) One thousand volts between live and dead metal parts of a motor.
c) Five hundred volts between a secondary circuit operating at 50 volts or less and dead metal parts; 1000 volts plus twice the maximum rated secondary circuit voltage between a secondary circuit, including any ferro-resonant windings, operating at more than 50 volts and dead metal parts.
d) One thousand volts plus the rated voltage of a capacitor between the terminals of a capacitor used for radio-interference elimination or arc suppression.
As an alternative, testing may be conducted using a direct current potential equal to the peak of the specified sinusoidal potential (1.414 times the sinusoidal rms value).

Name: UL 1564 32.2.2
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: While still heated, the primary winding is to be subjected to an alternating potential of twice the rated voltage at any acceptable frequency � typically 120 hertz or higher � for 7200 electrical cycles or for 60 seconds, whichever is less. The required test voltage is to be obtained by starting at one-quarter or less of the full value and increasing to the full value in not more than 15 seconds. After being held for the time specified, the voltage is to be reduced within 5 seconds to one-quarter or less of the maximum value, and the primary-winding circuit is to be opened.

Name: UL 1564 32.2.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: If a bobbin-wound transformer is required to be tested as provided in note (l) of Table 17.1 and item (d) of Exception to 17.2.3, after constant temperatures have been reached as the result of operation under the conditions specified in Temperature Test, Section 30, each of three separate samples of the transformer shall withstand without breakdown an induced potential test in accordance with 32.2.2 and 32.2.3.

Name: UL 1564 33.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
A product shall be conditioned for 24 hours in moist air having a relative humidity of 85�5 percent at a temperature of 32.0 �2.0�C (89.6 �3.6�F). After the conditioning:
a) A cord-connected product rated for a nominal 120-volt supply shall comply with Leakage- Current Test, Section 28. The circuit illustrated in Figure 33.1 shall be used in this tests, which may be discontinued when the leakage current stabilizes.
 b) A product other than as mentioned in (a) shall have an insulation resistance of 50,000 ohmsor more between live parts and interconnected dead metal parts.
c) All products shall withstand without breakdown for 1 minute the application of a 40 to 70 hertz essentially sinusoidal potential of 1000 volts, or a direct current potential of 1414 volts, between live parts and interconnected dead metal parts.

Name: UL 1564 42.3.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A product shall be placed on a concrete surface, and the longest edge shall be raised 6 inches (152.4 mm) as the product is tilted. The product shall then be allowed to fall freely onto the concrete surface. The entire product shall then be raised 2 inches (50.8 mm) in an upright position and allowed to fall freely onto the concrete surface.

Name: UL 1564 42.4.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A product shall be placed on a concrete surface and the front bottom edge raised until the product tips over. The product shall be allowed to fall freely onto the concrete surface.

Name: UL 1564 45.1
Author: SpencerSkelly

Name: UL 1564 33.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The isolation transformer in this circuit is provided to reduce the risk of electric shock to personnel conducting the test.

Name: UL 1564 33.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: Before conducting the leakage-current measurements described in 33.1 using the circuit illustrated in Figure 33.1, the product is to be disconnected from the receptacle and it is to be determined that stray currents are negligible by closing switch S1, utilizing both positions of switch S2, and observing the stray leakage on the meter.

Name: UL 1564 32.1.2
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: To determine whether a product complies with the requirements in 32.1.1, it is to be tested using a source of 500-volt-ampere capacity or larger, having an output voltage that can be varied. The applied potential is to be increased from zero until the required test level is reached, and is to be held at that level for 1 minute. The increase in applied potential is to be at a substantially uniform rate and as rapid as is consistent with correct indication of its value by a voltmeter.

Name: UL 1564 22.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A capacitor connected across the line, such as a capacitor for radio-interference elimination or power-factor correction, shall be housed within an enclosure or container that protects the plates against mechanical damage and prevents the emission of flame or molten material resulting from a malfunction or breakdown of the capacitor.

Name: UL 1564 Table 44.2 Bonding conductor short-circuit test
Author: SpencerSkelly

Name: UL 1564 44.3
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The fuse used for connection of the circuit described in 44.1 and 44.2 shall have a current rating equal to that of the branch circuit overcurrent device to which the equipment is connected, but not less than 20 amperes. Characteristics of the fuse are such that the fuse will not open in less than 12 seconds when carrying twice its rated current.

Name: UL 1564 Table 44.1 Duration of current flow
Author: SpencerSkelly

Name: UL 1564 44.2
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The circuit for the test described in 44.1(b) is to have a power factor of 0.9 - 1.0 and is to be limited to the current specified in Table 44.2 at the voltage specified in Table 27.1. The open-circuit voltage of the test circuit is to be 100 - 105 percent of the specified voltage. The circuit is to be connected through a non-renewable fuse described in 44.3. One test is to be performed on each of the three samples of the bonding conductor subject to the test.

Name: UL 1564 43.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A marking that is required to be permanent shall be molded, die-stamped, paint-stenciled, stamped, etched on metal, or another method that is permanently secured; or be a pressure-sensitive label secured by adhesive that complies with the requirements in the Standard for Marking and Labeling Systems, UL 969.

Name: UL 1564 44.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
A bonding conductor that does not comply with the requirement in 26.9 is acceptable if:
a) The bonding conductor does not open when carrying for the time specified in Table 44.1 a current that equals twice the branch-circuit overcurrent-device rating � see 44.3 � but not less than 40 amperes; and
b) None of three samples of the bonding conductor, selected at random, opens during a limited
short-circuit test with a current as specified in Table 44.2 when in series with a fuse as described in 44.2 and 44.3.

Name: UL 1564 20.5
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
An acceptably rated direct-current circuit breaker or fuse or fuses shall be provided in the output circuit of the battery charger for overcurrent protection against short-circuiting of the terminals and reverse polarity connection. See 39.1 � 39.3.
Exception: A protective circuit may be used in lieu of a circuit breaker or fuse provided the charger complies with the output short circuit and reverse polarity tests under any condition of a single component open or short fault in the protective circuit.

Name: UL 1564 20.6
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A fuse and fuseholder shall have voltage and current ratings acceptable for the circuit in which they are connected.

Name: UL 1564 20.3
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
A circuit breaker provided to comply with the requirement in 20.2 shall be a common trip type that automatically opens all ungrounded conductors of the input circuit under fault or overload conditions within the battery charger.
Exception: If the battery charger has provision for connection of a grounded neutral conductor, individual single-pole circuit breakers are acceptable as the protection for each ungrounded conductor of a 3-wire, single-phase circuit, or for each ungrounded conductor of a 4-wire, 3-phase circuit, provided that no conductor involves a potential to ground in excess of 150 volts.

Name: UL 1564 20.4
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A thermal cutoff or other device employed to reduce a risk of fire or electric shock due to overheating of a transformer during normal operation shall comply with the requirements applicable to such a device in addition to the applicable requirements in this standard � for example, a thermal cutoff shall comply with the applicable requirements in this Standard and those in the Standard for Thermal-Links � Requirements and Application Guide, UL 60691.

Name: UL 1564 20.9
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The screw shell of a plug-type fuseholder and the upper terminal of an extractor-type fuseholder shall be connected toward the load.

Name: UL 1564 20.7
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: If a fuseholder is accessible to the user, the fuse size shall be marked in accordance with 48.5.

Name: UL 1564 20.8
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: An uninsulated live part of a fuseholder, other than the screw shell or clips, that may increase the risk of an electric shock shall not be exposed to contact by a person removing or replacing the fuse.

Name: UL 1564 36.3
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: To determine if a secondary-circuit switch or other control device mentioned in the Exception to 19.1 complies with the requirements in the overload test, the product is to be connected to a supply circuit of rated frequency and maximum test voltage � see Table 27.1. The device is to be caused to make and break 150 percent of the rated secondary-load current. During the test, exposed dead metal parts of the product are to be connected to the polarity opposite to the switching devices through a 3-ampere plug fuse. The test is to be conducted as described in 36.2.

Name: UL 1564 36.2
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: To determine if a primary-circuit device performs acceptably while controlling its load, the product is to be connected to a grounded supply with the rotor of a motor locked in position and with the output load adjusted to 150 percent of the rated value. During the test, exposed dead metal parts of the product are to be connected to ground through a 3-ampere plug fuse, and the connection is to be such that any single-pole, current-rupturing device will be connected in the ungrounded conductor of the supply circuit. The device is to be operated for 50 cycles at a rate of not more than 10 cycles-per-minute, except that a faster rate of operation may be employed if agreeable to those concerned.

Name: UL 1564 34.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The strain relief means specified in 11.2.1 shall withstand for 1 minute without displacement a direct pull of 35 pounds (156 N) applied to the cord, as described in 34.2, with the connections in the product disconnected. The strain relief is not acceptable if, at the point of disconnection of the conductors, there is such movement of the cord or lead as to indicate that stress on the connections have resulted.

Name: UL 1564 Figure 33.1 Circuit for measuring leakage current after humidity conditioning
Author: SpencerSkelly

Name: UL 1564 35.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: To determine compliance with 11.2.3, a product shall be tested in accordance with 35.2 without occurrence of any of the conditions specified in or 11.2.3 (a) � (d).

Name: UL 1564 34.2
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A 35-pound (16 kg) weight is to be suspended from the cord and supported by the product so that the strain relief means is stressed from any angle the construction of the product permits.

Name: UL 1564 29.2
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
A product having an output rating of more than 20 amperes and intended to charge lead-acid storage batteries is to be tested with:
a) A resistive-capacitive (rc) load having capacitance of 100,000 microfarads;
b) A battery supplemented with a resistive load bank; or
c) An acceptable battery if requested by the manufacturer.

Name: UL 1564 29.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The input current and power factor to a product is to be measured with the charger operating while connected to the maximum rated load. The current input shall not be more than 110 percent of the rated value.

Name: UL 1564 Table 30.1 Maximum acceptable temperature rises
Author: SpencerSkelly

Name: UL 1564 30.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A product, tested as described in 30.2 � 30.11, using a load adjusted to the rated maximum load current as described in 30.2 and 30.3, shall not reach a temperature at any point high enough to cause a risk of fire, damage to any material used, or exceed the temperature rises specified in Table 30.1.

Name: UL 1564 36.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
If tests are required, a switch or other control device shall be subjected to the overload test without electrical or mechanical malfunction or breakdown. The performance is unacceptable if:
a) The fuse in the grounding connection opens during the test;
b) There is welding of contacts or mechanism breakdown; or
c) The device is otherwise incapable of completing the test.

Name: UL 1564 35.2
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The supply cord or lead is to be held 1 inch (25.4 mm) from the point where the cord or lead emerges from the product and is then to be pushed back into the product. When a removable bushing which extends further than 1 inch is present, it is to be removed prior to the test. When the bushing is an integral part of the cord, the test is to be carried out by holding the bushing. The cord or lead is to be pushed back into the product in 1-inch (25.4-mm) increments until the cord buckles or the force to push the cord into the product exceed 6 pounds-force (26.7 N). The supply cord or lead within the product is to be manipulated to determine compliance with 11.2.3.

Name: UL 1564 40.1.2
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
For a product having multitap positions, the tests described in 40.1.1 shall be conducted at more than one setting of output-voltage or current rating or both, to represent the most severe operating condition.
Exception: Tests may be conducted at only one position if that position represents the most severe condition.

Name: UL 1564 40.1.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A product shall not emit flame or molten metal or result in a risk of fire or electric shock while operating as described in the temperature test, except under the burnout conditions described in 40.2.1. With reference to 40.3.1, the burnout test of the transformer shall be followed by a dielectric voltage-withstand test, as required by 32.1.1(a), applied between the primary and secondary windings of the transformer and between the primary winding and accessible dead metal parts of the transformer.

Name: UL 1564 39.5.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A product that is intended for operation with two or more supply-voltage levels or with a varying number of battery cells or both, shall be connected in such a way as to produce the most adverse conditions when connected to the highest alternating-current input voltage specified for the charger. For example, 440 volts plus 10 percent on a 220-volt tap with the product connected for 12-cell charging to a six-cell battery. The product is to be connected to a discharged battery, all normally supplied protective devices are to be left in the circuit, and the product is then to be energized. The test is to be continued until the internal protection opens, constant temperatures are attained, or the circuitry opens. If an automatically reset protector is provided, the test is to be continued for 7 hours. A manually reset protector is to be operated for 50 cycles.

Name: UL 1564 46.3
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: Any acceptable indicating device � an ohmmeter, battery-and-buzzer combination, or the like � may be used to determine whether a product complies with the requirement in 46.1.

Name: UL 1564 29.4
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: Output current measurements of either half-wave or full-wave rectified circuits are to be based on the average current.

Name: UL 1564 29.3
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: With reference to 29.2(c), if a product is to be tested using a battery or batteries as the load, the size of the battery is to be of the size indicated by the 8 hour rating marked on the product�s nameplate. The battery is to be connected to the proper load and then discharged to 1.70 volts per cell at a rate not exceeding the discharge rate assigned by the battery manufacturer, and not exceeding one-sixth of the ampere-hour capacity of the battery.

Name: UL 1564 42.1.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: There shall not be a reduction of spacings beyond the minimum acceptable level or exposure of a live part that presents a risk of electric shock when a product is subjected to the tests described in 42.2 � 42.4. The tests described in 42.3 and 42.4 apply only to single-circuit industrial truck battery chargers, and the tests are to be on a completely assembled and packaged charger. The rod described in 7.2 is to be used to determine whether a live part that presents a risk of electric shock is exposed.

Name: UL 1564 40.3.2
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The overcurrent protection specified in the Exception to 40.3.1 shall not trip the three successive on-off operations of the product at intervals of not more than 5 seconds under full-load conditions.

Name: UL 1564 40.3.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
A resistive load that causes the primary to draw three times the alternating current obtained during normal operation � see 29.1 and Table 27.1 � is to be connected directly to the transformer secondary winding with the product connected to a supply circuit at 100 percent of the maximum test voltage � see Table 27.1. For a transformer having a center tap secondary, a single load is to be connected across the legs of the winding that result in the greatest potential. During the test, the product enclosure is to be connected directly to ground. The transformer is to be operated continuously:
a) Until the ultimate conditions are observed;
b) For 7 hours if cycling of an automatically reset protector occurs; or
c) For 50 cycles of resetting a manually reset protector.
Exception No. 1: The test need not be conducted if over-current protection rated at least 125 percent, but not exceeding 150 percent, of the rated input current is provided by:
a) Internal input-circuit protection; or
b) Branch-circuit protection as marked on the product in accordance with 49.8.
Exception No. 2: A transformer employed in a switch-mode inverter or converter circuit may be subjected to the transformer overload test described in 40.3.5 in lieu of the transformer burnout test.

Name: UL 1564 40.2.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: An electromagnetic relay or a solenoid having an open-coil construction is to be tested by blocking the armature or the plunger in the de-energized position. The product is then to be operated until burnout of the coil occurs or the temperatures become constant. During the test, the product enclosure is to be connected directly to ground.

Name: UL 1564 40.1.3
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A burnout test may be concluded by the opening of branch-circuit overcurrent protection if the product is marked in accordance with 49.8.

Name: UL 1564 30.5
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A product designed for mounting or support in more than one position, or in a confined location, is to be tested in a manner representing the most severe conditions. An adjacent mounting or supporting surface is to consist of 1-inch thick, soft-pine boards.

Name: UL 1564 30.2
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: With reference to 29.1, if the load is comprised of a battery supplemented with a resistive load in accordance with 29.2(b), the manufacturer shall provide the characteristic charge curve for the product. The resistor is to be adjusted throughout the charging period so that the current follows the characteristic charge curve during the temperature test.

Name: UL 1564 30.3
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
With reference to 30.2, in the temperature test of a product using a battery load, the battery shall be discharged as indicated in 29.3 then charged until temperatures on the product reach a maximum and begin to decrease. The temperature test is then to be continued using a second battery, also discharged as indicated in 29.3, until maximum temperatures are attained. A product provided with a timer and a marked charging time based on the ampere-hour capacity of the battery is to be tested for the marked time period.
Exception: A second battery is not used for products which provide a constant charging current or have a marked charging time such that only one battery can be charged during an 8-hour period.

Name: UL 1564 30.10
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A thermocouple junction and adjacent thermocouple lead wires are to be securely held in thermal contact with the surface of the material being measured. In most cases, adequate thermal contact results from securely taping or cementing the thermocouple in place, but if a metal surface is involved, brazing or soldering of the thermocouple to the metal may be necessary.

Name: UL 1564 30.11
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: For a test that is to be continued until constant temperatures are attained, thermal equilibrium is considered to exist when three successive readings taken at intervals of 10 percent of the previously elapsed duration of the test, but not less than 5 minutes, indicate no further increase.

Name: UL 1564 42.2.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A sheet-metal enclosure having a thickness less than that required by 6.3 � 6.8 is to be subjected to an impact of 5 foot-pounds (6.78 J) using a 2-inch (50.8-mm) diameter steel ball.

Name: UL 1564 30.8
Author: SpencerSkelly

Name: UL 1564 30.9
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
Thermocouples are to consist of wires not larger than 24 AWG (0.21 mm2) and not smaller than 30
AWG (0.05 mm2). When thermocouples are used in determining temperatures in electrical equipment, it
is common practice to employ thermocouples consisting of 30 AWG iron and constantan wire and a
potentiometer type instrument. Such equipment is to be used whenever referee temperature
measurements by thermocouples are necessary. The thermocouples and related instruments are to be
accurate and calibrated in accordance with good laboratory practice. The thermocouple wire is to conform
with the requirements specified in the Initial Calibration Tolerances for Thermocouples table in
Temperature Measurement Thermocouples, ANSI/ISA MC96.1.

Name: UL 1564 30.6
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: All values of temperature rise in Table 30.1 are based on an assumed ambient temperature of 25�C (77�F). However, tests may be conducted at any ambient temperature within the range of 10 � 40�C (50 � 104�F).

Name: UL 1564 30.7
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
Coil and winding temperatures are to be measured by thermocouples located on exposed surfaces, except that the resistance method may be used for a coil that is inaccessible for mounting thermocouples, such as a coil:
a) Immersed in sealing compound;
b) Wrapped with thermal insulation such as asbestos; or
c) Wrapped with more than two layers of material, such as cotton, paper, or rayon more than 1/32 inch (0.8 mm) thick.
In an alternating-current motor, the thermocouple is to be mounted on the integrally applied insulation of the coil wire.

The meter used need not have all the attributes of the defined instrument.
a) The meter is to have an input impedance of 1500 ohms resistance shunted by a capacitance of 0.15 microfarad.
b) The meter is to indicate 1.11 times the average of the full-wave rectified composite waveform of voltage across the resistor or current through the resistor.
c) Over a frequency range of 0 � 100 kilohertz, the measurement circuit is to have a frequency response � ratio of indicated to actual value of current � that is equal to the ratio of the impedance of a 1500 ohm resistor shunted by a 0.15 microfarad capacitor to 1500 ohms. At an indication of 0.5 or 0.75 milliampere, the measurement is to have an error of not more than 5 percent at 60 hertz.

Name: UL 1564 27.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
A representative sample of a product shall be subjected to the tests described in Sections 27 - 44.
Unless otherwise specified, all tests are to be conducted at the voltage specified in Table 27.1. A product
rated 50 - 60 hertz is to be tested at 60 hertz.

Name: UL 1564 28.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
The leakage current of a cord-connected power unit when tested in accordance with 28.2 � 28.6 shall not be more than:
a) 0.5 milliampere for a portable power unit; or
b) 0.75 milliampere for a stationary power unit.
Exception: A unit having primary-circuit filtering shall have higher leakage current levels at accessible parts, only when the unit complies with the following:
a) Leakage current does not exceed 5.0 milliampere and the unit complies with the grounding requirements in Section 25, Grounding; or
b) Leakage current does not exceed 5 percent of the input current determined in accordance with Section 29, Power Input Test, and all of the following conditions are met:
1) The unit complies with the grounding requirements in Section 25, Grounding;
2) The unit is not supplied through a standard configuration 125 volt, 15 amp nor 125 volt, 20 amp non-locking type plug; and
3) Provision is made for connecting together and earth-grounding all the metal frames of the unit in the system.

Name: UL 1564 28.2
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: All exposed conductive surfaces are to be tested for leakage currents. The leakage currents from these surfaces are to be measured to the grounded supply conductor individually as well as collectively if simultaneously accessible, and from one surface to another if simultaneously accessible. Parts are considered to be exposed surfaces unless guarded by an enclosure considered acceptable as defined in 7.2 to reduce the risk of an electric shock. Surfaces are considered to be simultaneously accessible if they can be readily contacted by one or both hands of a person at the same time. These measurements do not apply between output terminals operating at voltage less than 30 volts rms � 42.4 volts peak.

Name: UL 1564 28.3
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: If a conductive surface other than metal is used for the enclosure or part of the enclosure, the leakage current is to be measured using a metal foil with an area of 10 by 20 centimeters in contact with the surface. If the surface has an area less than 10 by 20 centimeters, the metal foil is to be the same size as the surface. The metal foil is not to remain in place long enough to affect the temperature of the product.

Name: UL 1564 37.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: The impedance at 60 hertz between the point of connection of the equipment-grounding means and any other metal part that is required to be grounded (see Section 25, Grounding) shall not be more than 0.1 ohm when measured in accordance with 37.2.

Name: UL 1564 31.2
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
The rated output current of the product is to be continuously maintained by an adjustable resistor connected in parallel with the battery. The test is to be continued:
a) Until ultimate conditions are observed;
b) For 7 hours if cycling of an automatically reset protector occurs; or
c) For 50 cycles of resetting a manually reset protector.

Name: UL 1564 31.1
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
A product tested using a battery as a load as described in 30.3 shall be subjected to an intermediate abnormal test described in 31.2 immediately following the temperature test. The product shall not emit flame or molten metal or result in a risk of fire or electric shock during the test. The test is to be followed by a dielectric voltage-withstand test, as required by 32.1.1(a), applied between the primary and secondary windings of the transformer.
Exception: A product that is current limited during normal charging is not required to be subjected to a continuous load test.

Name: UL 1564 40.3.3
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A ferro-resonant transformer is to be tested as described in 40.3.1, except that a resistive load that draws the maximum power input � see Power Input Test, Section 29 � is to be connected directly to the transformer secondary winding, with the product connected to a supply circuit at 106 percent of the maximum test voltage specified in Table 27.1.

Name: UL 1564 40.3.4
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: A transformer supplying a low-voltage circuit as described in 24.4.1 is to be tested in the same manner as a Class 2 transformer, with low-voltage wiring terminals short-circuited, and wiring not conforming to 14.1 short-circuited. A transformer supplying an isolated-limited-power circuit as described in 24.4.1 is to be tested with all secondary windings directly short-circuited. If a portion of an isolated-limited-power circuit is connected to low-voltage, field-wiring terminals, separate samples are to be subjected to the Class 2 transformer test and the shorted-secondary test.

Name: UL 1564 40.3.5
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
In reference to Exception No. 2 to 40.3.1, the power circuit supplied by the transformer is to be connected to a resistive load that draws maximum obtainable current without:
a) Causing operation of internal overcurrent protection devices or a protection circuit; or
b) Resulting in opening of a circuit component, such as a diode, resistor, solid state device, or similar component.

Name: UL 1564 28.7
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: Normally the complete leakage current test program as described in 28.6 is to be conducted without interruption for other tests. With the concurrence of those concerned, the leakage current test may be interrupted to conduct other nondestructive tests.

Name: UL 1564 28.6
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note:
A sample of the product is to be tested for leakage current starting with the as-received condition � the as-received condition is without prior energizing, except as may occur as part of the production-line testing � but with the grounding conductor, if any, open at the attachment plug. The supply voltage is to be adjusted to the voltage specified in Table 27.1. The test sequence, with reference to the measuring circuit, Figure 28.1, is to be as follows:
a) With switch S1 open, the product is to be without load and connected to the measuring circuit. The leakage current is to be measured using both positions of switch S2 and with the product switching devices in all their normal operating positions.
b) Switch S1 is then to be closed, energizing the product, and within 5 seconds the leakage current is to be measured using both positions of switch S2, with the product switching devices in all their normal operating positions.
c) The leakage current is to be monitored, using both positions of switch S2, until thermal stabilization is attained by operating the product as in the temperature test.

Name: UL 1564 28.5
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: Unless the meter is being used to measure leakage from one part of a product to another, the meter is to be connected between an accessible part and the grounded supply conductor.

Name: UL 1564 37.2
Author: SpencerSkelly
Note: Compliance with 37.1 is to be determined by measuring the voltage when a current of 25 amperes derived from a 60 hertz source with a no-load voltage not exceeding 6 volts is passed between the grounding connection and the metal part in question.

Name: SAE ARP1816E 01. SCOPE
Author: skellys
Note:
This SAE Aerospace Recommended Practice (ARP) describes three general types of Ground Support Equipment (GSE) industrial battery chargers. The battery charger typically requiring up to 8 hours to recharge a 100% discharged battery, hereafter called �Conventional Charger.� A charger, hereafter called �Opportunity Charger,� which has the ability to charge at a slightly faster rate than a conventional charger. A charger, hereafter called �Fast Charger,� which has the ability to charge at a much faster rate than a conventional charger. Recommendations that apply to all types will refer generically to �charger.�
This document does not include an information in reference to on-board chargers powered by external AC power sources such as Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) or Level III automotive style DC fast chargers.

Name: 2.1.4.1 Pre-Charge Time
Author: skellys

Name: 2.1.4.2 Pre-Charge Fault Tolerance

  • A green status indicator when no faults are present in the unit and the DC Bus is ready.
  • A red status indicator that shows a thermal fault has occurred.

Author: skellys

Author: skellys

The power disconnect shall be a mechanical configuration and shall remove power from all internal circuits.  The power disconnect shall be an optional component.

Name: 2.7.4 Control Interface Wiring
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall have a terminal block and wiring box consistent with UL and/or NEC requirements.  In addition the wiring terminals shall be installed and maintained with standard electrician tools.

Name: 2.7.5 Control Interface Function
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall provide two terminals for control of the main contactor and two terminals for control of the pre-charge circuit.  Both circuits shall be active when the terminals are shorted by contacts located in the master MVS Station.

Name: 2.7.6 Control Interface Specification
Author: skellys
Note:
The open circuit voltage for the control interface shall be one hundred twenty volts AC nominal. The minimum current required to activate the control interface functions shall be less than fifty milli-amps.  The maximum current allowed for the interface circuit shall be five amps.
The master MVS Station shall be required to have contacts rated for a minimum of two hundred milli-amps and a maximum rating of five amps.

Name: 2.7.7 Housekeeping Power
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall provide one hundred twenty volts AC nominal at a power rating of twelve hundred watts.  This power source shall be capable of sustaining a short in the wiring conduit and shall not damage the MVS Server.  Replacement of a fusing device is acceptable.

Note: The enclosure shall be rated NEMA 2.

Name: 2.6.5 Corrosion Resistance
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall have corrosion resistance on all metal surfaces.  The finish for corrosion resistance shall be Zinc Plate type II (gold) SC3 IAW ASTM B633.

Name: 2.4.4 Thermal Monitoring
Author: skellys
Note: MVS Server shall include sensors on all magnetic components and semiconductors and shall disable operation of the MVS Server if these temperatures are above the design rating.  No other protective monitoring shall be included in the MVS Server.

Name: 2.4.5 Isolation
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall include a dielectric isolation barrier.  The isolation barrier shall comply with the designated UL and cUL requirements for this type of barrier.

Name: 2.4.6 Mean Time Between Failures
Author: skellys
Note: The MTBF shall be a minimum of twenty thousand hours.  The MTBF shall be verified by MIL-Handbook-217 method.

Name: 2.5.1 Physical Size Constraint
Author: skellys
Note: The maximum physical size of the MVS Server shall be 60" high, 42" wide, and 27" deep.  The maximum buildup of the MVS Server from the wall surface shall be thirty inches.  This shall include any protruding lamps or switch assemblies.

Name: 2.5.2 Paint Requirement
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall be power coated on TBD surfaces.  The paint shall be Corvel TGIC Polysters ANSI 70 GRAY, 30-7065, GLOSS:60-70-U.L.

Name: 2.5.3 Installation Limitation
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall be designed for installation distances as short as six inches from one side (either), and the rear of the unit.

Name: 2.5.4 Mean Time To Service
Author: skellys
Note: The MTTS shall be five minutes when completed by trained facilities personnel.  This shall be verified by timing all user serviceable part repairs and demonstrating compliance.  The longest time to repair shall be less than ten minutes.

Name: 2.5.5 Mean Time To Repair
Author: skellys
Note: The MTTR shall be one hour when completed by a trained field service technician or engineer.  This shall be verified by identifying field repairable parts and demonstrating compliance.  The Isolation Transformer contained in the MVS Server is excluded from this requirement.

Name: 2.3.2 DC Output Monitoring
Author: skellys
Note: The DC output voltage shall not be monitored for faults or operability.  A Pre-charge lockout shall prevent damage from occurring to the server or stations when inadequate time is given for pre-charge to complete.  The lockout function shall be verified by observing that the output current does not exceed the rated output current when the maximum specified number of stations are connected and all enables are applied simultaneously.

Name: 2.3.3 Fault Tolerance
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall be capable of withstanding faults applied as a result of wiring errors introduced during installation. An external and Operating-Manual-specified circuit breaker is mandatory for this testing.  Resetting of this external circuit breaker shall be allowed to restart the unit.  The faults shall be applied for a minimum of one second to verify this requirement.  A failed component shall not be allowed during this test.

Name: 2.3.5 Output Current
Author: skellys
Note: Maximum current will occur at the minimum specified line condition.  At this condition the MVS Server shall be capable of supplying the full specified power.

Name: 2.3.6 Output Ripple Current
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall have no more than ten percent ripple.   Ripple shall be measured as the AC RMS component divided by the DC output current.  These measurements shall be made at nominal load and line conditions.

Name: 2.4.1 Safety Agency Approval
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall be listed under the UL specification UL1012 Power Supplies at 480 VAC input.  The MVS Server shall also be approved under the CSA (cUL) specification  CSA22.2 no. 107, at 480 and 600 VAC input

Name: 2.4.2 FMEA
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall be analyzed using standard FMEA methods.  The FMEA results shall be communicated to the design team in a formal review.

Name: 2.4.3 Sags, Surges, and Strikes
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall be designed and tested for compliance with UL991.

Name: 2.1.5 Efficiency Requirement
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall have a measured efficiency of greater than ninety percent at loads greater than fifty percent of rating.  Test conditions shall be at nominal line and load conditions.  The efficiency shall be measured from the AC input terminals to the DC output terminals.

Name: 2.2.1 Rated Voltage Range
Author: skellys
Note: The input rated voltage shall be 480 VAC and 600 VAC.  The MVS Server shall be designed for configuration at either voltage as a nominal value. The tolerance for input voltage shall be plus ten percent to minus fifteen percent as a nominal range.  No performance degradation shall be allowed over this operating range.

Name: 2.2.2 Input Voltage Monitoring
Author: skellys
Note: The input voltage shall not be monitored for input frequency or amplitude.

Name: 2.2.3 Power Factor
Author: skellys
Note: The input power factor for the MVS Server shall be greater than .9

Name: 2.2.4 Harmonic Distortion
Author: skellys
Note: Measured harmonic distortion shall be less than twenty five percent at nominal output load and input voltage.

Name: 2.2.5 Operating Frequency
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall be compatible with sixty-Hertz utilities.  All performance testing shall be conducted at sixty Hertz.

Name: 2.2.6 Terminal Block
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall have an input terminal block for connection of utility wiring.  The terminal block shall be rated for the operating current and voltage for the MVS Server.

Name: 2.3.1 Rated Output Voltage Range
Author: skellys
Note: The minimum DC output voltage shall be 137 volts DC.  The maximum DC output voltage shall be 170 volts DC.  The minimum voltage shall be measured under a low line condition at full load.  The maximum voltage shall be measured at ten percent load at maximum line.

Name: 1 SCOPE
Author: skellys
Note:
This specification sets the design requirements for the second-generation power server for the Multi-Vehicle Battery Charging System or MVS. The MVS Server will be replacing the existing server based on the PosiCharge product.  The MVS consists of a Power Server and Power Stations that are used to charge industrial electric vehicles.

The MVS Server contains all necessary components to isolate and distribute the required voltages to the MVS Charging Stations.  This document shall provide all necessary requirements to design and test the first article MVS Server.  All pertinent issues shall be covered in this document and adhered to by the design team.  The engineering authority for this product shall approve deviations from this specification.  Points of contact shall be Bill Conn and Darrell Buchanan.

Name: 2.1.1 Maximum Power Rating
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall be capable of supplying eighty kilowatts, continuous, at the specified voltage range and maximum ambient.

Name: 2.1.2 Reduced Power Capability
Author: skellys
Note: The MVS Server shall have a nameplate power code.  This power code shall not contain any intelligent data but shall be randomly generated. The power code shall indicate a rating that is used in the Master Power Server in the same system and shall be used to set the power rating for the system.  The codes for power rating shall be TBD.

Name: 2.1.3 Backward Compatibility
Author: skellys
Note:
The MVS Server shall be compatible with existing installations using the previous generation server. The changes allowable to the system to facilitate this shall be limited to:
  • Replacement of the MVS Station(s) software.
  • Addition of an accessory driver board.
  • MVS Server power ratings must match.
Verification of this requirement shall be met by installation in an existing sight, by trained field-service personnel, with the changes allowed.

Name: 2.1.4 System Pre-Charge
Author: skellys
Note: Pre-charge is the process of raising the output to an operating level prior to activating the main power components.  The MVS Server shall provide the DC output pre-charge for the MVS Stations

Name: 2.6.5.1 Temperature Fold-back
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall decrease the output power to prevent internal component failures should a blocked fan or failed fan condition arise.  Discreet fold-back or shutdown shall be an acceptable implementation of this requirement

Name: Human Readable Markings
Author: skellys
Note: Markings shall be human readable from the distance expected in the use case

Name: Schedule EQ Charge
Author: skellys
Note: Theauthorized user shall be able to schedule or unschedule an equalization (EQ) charge event from the remote HMI, specifying the start time, and the system shall initiate the EQ charge automatically at the scheduled time without further user intervention.

Author: skellys
Note: This chip resets and does not allow SW to load

Name: 2.2.6.3 PosiNET – Ethernet Interface
Author: skellys
Note: The DVS100 and DVS150 shall have the PosiNET Compatible Kit available for customers to be purchased and installed by field service personnel. PosiNET is a fleet management system for industrial electric vehicles, the data collected by the chargers are transmitted through an internal network to a remote transmission unit (RTU) which aggregates real time and historical data and passes it along secured internet connections to an offsite, back-end database system where the data is stored and analyzed. This kit shall not ship as part of the baseline configuration.

Name: 2.4.3.2 Current Stability - NMS
Author: skellys
Note: The accuracy and resolution of the current output shall not vary more than 1% over the specified operating temperature range of the product.

Name: 2.4.3.3 Current Calibration - NMS
Author: skellys
Note: The power stage shall include a provision for calibration of current offset.  This is required to ensure accurate current delivery even at currents below 10 amps.

Name: 2.4.7.1 Modular Connector Position
Author: skellys
Note:
The Port A connector location will be in a vertical position located on the left side of the charger. as viewed from the front,  
The Port B connector location will be in a vertical position located on the right side of the charger, as viewed from the front,

Name: 2.2.1.1 Control Power – IPC Control Board
Author: skellys
Note:
The charger shall supply control power for the PosiCharge control board.  The control power shall be routed to the front panel along with the other interfaces in the final charger configuration.  The control power shall be present whenever the battery charger is turned to the “On” state.  The control power shall be isolated from high voltage circuitry with UL compliant voltage isolation and shall supply the following power supply voltages and currents:
+15VDC @ 2 ADC
-15VDC @ 1 ADC
+5VDC @ 5 ADC

Name: 2.2.1.2 Output Current Control Resolution
Author: skellys
Note:
Output Current / Output Resolution
0-50A / 1A
51-250A / 2A

Name: 2.2.1.3 Constant-Power Regulation
Author: skellys
Note: The PosiCharge control board shall manage the constant power functionality of the final product. The charger shall measure current and voltage operating conditions, at the output terminals, and shall adjust the current command to prevent operating conditions from exceeding the maximum specified power for the charger.

Name: 2.2.5.1 Control Power – Accessory Driver Kit
Author: skellys
Note:
The charger shall supply control power for the two (2) accessory driver kits. The control power shall be routed to the accessory driver kit interface. The control power shall be present whenever the battery charger is turned to the “On” state. The control power shall be capable of withstanding a short across the power with no blown fuses or damage to components. The control power shall be isolated from high voltage circuitry with UL compliant voltage isolation and shall supply the following power supply voltages and currents:
  • 24VAC @ 2A rms AC
  • Short Circuit current shall be less than 5A rms AC
  • Open Circuit voltage shall be less than 35VAC

Name: 2.2.6.1 Control Power – RS-422 Interface
Author: skellys
Note:
The charger shall supply control power for two (2) optional RS-422 Interface electronics. The control power shall be routed to the interface connector along with the isolated serial communication wiring. The control power shall be present whenever the battery charger is turned to the “On” state. The control power shall be isolated from high voltage circuitry with UL compliant voltage isolation and shall supply meet the following specifications:
  • 24VAC +/- 20%
  • 0 to 500mA rms AC
  • Short Circuit and Overload Protected

Name: 2.2.6.2 Champ Compatible Kit
Author: skellys
Note: The DVS100 and DVS150 shall have the Champ Compatible Kit available to customers to be purchased and installed by field service personnel. This kit shall not ship as part of the baseline configuration.

Name: 2.6.16 Humidity Pre-Conditioning before Hipot - NMS
Author: skellys
Note:
A product shall be conditioned for 24 hours in moist air having a relative humidity of 85±5 percent
at a temperature of 32.0 ±2.0°C (89.6 ±3.6°F). Hipot perform after the conditioning:  A product other than as mentioned in (a) shall have an insulation resistance of 50,000 ohms or more between live parts and interconnected dead metal parts.

Name: 2.7.1 Spare Parts Administration
Author: skellys
Note: The charger vendor shall recommend and assist with the development of a Spare Parts Administration program.  This program shall be administered by Customer Service.

Name: 2.7.2 Vendor Warranty
Author: skellys
Note:
The following warranty shall be supplied with the charger:
  • 2 Years on control electronics
  • 5 Years on power stage components
  • 10 Years on main transformer
  • 1 Year labor

Name: 2.7.3 Product Manuals
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall have a full set of manuals at the time of fielding the product. The manuals shall include installation, operation and maintenance versions and will be provided with each product shipment. North America to include the following languages - English, Spanish, French International to include the following languages- English, Spanish, French, German

Name: 2.7.4 Internal Labels
Author: skellys
Note: All internal and external labels and warnings shall be in the charger in the English language, as the standard configuration, and shall use international symbols.

Name: 2.7.5 External Labels
Author: skellys
Note: All internal and external labels and warnings shall be in the charger in the English language, as the standard configuration, and shall use international symbols.

Name: 2.6.10 Input Voltage Mismatch
Author: skellys
Note: A product that is intended for operation with two or more supply-voltage levels or with a varying number of battery cells or both, shall be connected in such a way as to produce the most adverse conditions when connected to the highest alternating-current input voltage specified for the charger. For example, 600 volts plus 10 percent on a 480-volt tap with the product connected for 12-cell charging to a eight-cell battery. The product is to be connected to a discharged battery, all normally supplied protective devices are to be left in the circuit, and the product is then to be energized. The test is to be continued until the internal protection opens, constant temperatures are attained, or the circuitry opens. If an automatically reset protector is provided, the test is to be continued for 7 hours. A manually reset protector is to be operated for 50 cycles.

Name: 2.6.11 Short Circuit
Author: skellys
Note: The DVS100 and DVS150 shall be designed to withstand an output short circuit during normal operation at full load. The DVS100 and DVS150 shall successfully recover upon removal of short circuit condition.

Name: 2.6.12 Reverse Battery
Author: skellys
Note: The DVS100 and DVS150 charger shall be capable of withstanding reverse connection of battery voltage to 150VDC. The charger shall not be damaged due to reverse wiring errors in the output power cables or connectors. Upon correction of the wiring errors the power supply shall resume charging.

Name: 2.6.13 Anti-Arcing Specification
Author: skellys
Note: The charger interface shall support rapid shut down to prevent connector anti-arcing. From loss of Pilot to output current below 5 ADC shall be 15 milli-seconds or less. The shut down can be implemented via the current command or digital enable line. Note:The PosiCharge control board takes 5 milli-seconds to process the pilot signal.

Name: 2.6.14 Loss of Phase
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall support rapid shutdown at the detection of loss of one or more phases prior to charging and loss while charging. Shall require 12 pulse design.

Name: 2.6.15 Emergency Power Off (EPO)
Author: skellys
Note: The function of the EPO switch is to quickly disconnect both the AC and DC power circuits. The charger shall provide an EPO switch operation. After an Emergency Power Off the EPO switch is manually reset by pulling and latching, the charger shall not turn “On” until the “Restart” button is pressed or power has been recycled (On/Off).

Name: 2.6.03 Failure Modes- NMS
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall not have any failure modes that allow continuous operation above the current or voltage command levels.  Disabling the charger via the enable line shall cause the output current to return to zero with all single failure modes considered.

Name: 2.6.04 Over Current Protection
Author: skellys
Note: The charger documentation shall specify AC Input fusing or a circuit breaker suitable for it’s rating in the product documentation.

Name: 2.6.05 Operating Temperature Range
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall operate, within the specified requirements, from –25C to +45C.

Name: 2.6.06 Storage Temperature Range
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall have a storage temperature range from –32C to +65C.

Name: 2.6.07 Reliability
Author: skellys
Note: The charger vendor shall supply reliability data for the model chosen once the final charger configuration has been identified.  The reliability (MTBF) goal for the product is 80,000 hours.

Name: 2.6.08 California Energy Commission Appliance Efficiency Standards Certification
Author: skellys
Note: Chargers with CEC option shall be certified to meet efficiency standards for large battery chargers specified by CEC-400-2012-011-CMF.

Name: 2.6.09 UL Approval
Author: skellys
Note: The vendor shall have the charger approved with the listing of UL 1564 and an equivalent c/UL rating.  The vendor shall obtain this listing in the final configuration with the PosiCharge control board and front panel.

Name: 2.5.13 Installation Stacking – N/A
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall be capable of stacking two high at the time of installation.  This is to facilitate better utilization of factory floor space.  This requirement can be implemented using a kit and external frame approach.  The requirement shall be implemented as a product option available to customers at the time of purchase.

Name: 2.5.14 Installation Area – N/A
Author: skellys
Note: The DVS100 / DVS150 shall support a wall mount installation. All cooling shall be achieved either through the front panel or the side panels.

Name: 2.5.15 Forklift Handling
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall have forklift-handling features suitable for assisting charger installation.

Name: 2.5.16 Safety Ground Connection
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall have provision for making a ground connection that meets the requirements of UL and NEC.

Name: 2.5.17 Mean Time to Repair
Author: skellys
Note: The MTTR of the DVS100 and DVS150 shall be 30 minutes, when completed by a single trained field service technician or PosiCharge certified forklift shop mechanic.

Name: 2.5.18 Easily replaceable Internal Components
Author: skellys
Note: The DVS100 and DVS150 shall, be designed with easy access to internal components. All major field-replaceable units that carry voltage (Ex. Power stage, control board) shall indicate failure by means of an LED or visible fault indicator.

Name: 2.5.19 Simplified Assembly and Troubleshooting
Author: skellys
Note: The DVS100 and DVS150 shall be designed for simple assembly and troubleshooting with common field service equipment. Design for manufacturing shall be coordinated with manufacturing and this requirement shall be met by approval from the manufacturing engineer at the producibility review.

Name: 2.6.01 EMI/EMC Requirements – North America
Author: skellys
Note: The DVS100 / DVS150 shall include all EMI/EMC components required within the chassis of the unit. The DVS100 / DVS150 shall be designed to meet the Electromagnetic Interference requirements for FCC class A Industrial equipment.

Name: 2.5.05 Color and Finish
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall be supplied with a powder coat finish.  The finish shall be CORVEL TGIC POLYESTERS ANSI 70 GREY, 30-7065, GLOSS:60-70-U.L. Also, available orange color cabinet option Pantone 1665 / RAL2004 (CMYK C:0 M:73 Y:100 K:0).

Name: 2.5.06 PosiCharge Logo
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall be supplied with a PosiCharge logo sticker per PosiCharge design documents that shall be affixed to the charger at the time of manufacture.  The location of the sticker shall be on the top right corner of Control Panel Assembly “A”.

Name: 2.5.07 PosiCharge Front Panel
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall feature two Bassi regulation boards and two Posicharge front panel assemblies. The Control Panel for Port A is to be mounted above the Control Panel for Port B.  A label “A” is to be located on the left side of Port A Control Panel Assembly.  A Label “B” is to be located on the right side of Port B Control Panel Assembly.

Name: 2.5.08 Fused Disconnect Mounting Option – N/A
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall support an optional fused disconnect which can be ordered at the time of manufacture.  This option may be implemented using either a fused-disconnect assembly or remotely activated relay assembly.  Either option shall preclude entry into the charger when in the operate switch position.

Name: 2.5.09 Accessory Driver Kit
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall have two (2) Accessory Driver Kits installed with the required terminal block, wiring harness, and knockout used for installing stack lights, water and ventilation accessories.

Name: 2.5.10 External RS-422 Interface Option
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall support a mounting location and provisions for mounting an optional external RS-422 Interface device.   In addition to the mounting of the RS-422 Interface device, mounting provisions for the Serial Isolation device, and a connector location shall also be supported.

Name: 2.5.11 Pogo-Stick Mounting Option – N/A
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall support a mounting location and provisions for mounting an optional pogo stick for cable management on the exterior of the charger.

Name: 2.5.12 Shipping Container
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall be packaged in a shipping container suitable for optimization of packing density for overseas shipment.  Details of shipping configuration to be mutually agreed between Posicharge and Bassi.

Name: 2.4.5 Duty Cycle
Author: skellys
Note: To meet the Maximum Power Rating and associated Current Range listed in section 2.4.3, 100% duty cycle shall be implemented.

Name: 2.4.6 Regulation Modes - NMS
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall automatically perform current and voltage regulation based on the supplied command and defined voltage limit.  The charger output voltage limit shall be 130VDC.  If the output voltage is below 130VDC then the power supply shall regulate output current based on the current command and the power limit.

Name: 2.4.7 Output Connection
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall be supplied with the connectors in place (UL1564 requires this).

Name: 2.4.8 Output Cable Length
Author: skellys
Note: Two 13 ft Output Cables to be supplied with each charger.  Cables shall have an Anderson Euro Connector on one end to mate to the charger and the other end is customer selectable; Anderson Euro or Schaltbau Euro.

Name: 2.5.01 Nema Rating
Author: skellys
Note: The charger enclosure shall have a rating of Nema 1.

Name: 2.5.02 Physical Size
Author: skellys
Note: The maximum physical size of the DVS100 and DVS150 shall be 51.47" high, 24.5" wide, and 20.44" deep.

Name: 2.5.03 Weight
Author: skellys
Note: The DVS100 shall weigh no more than 529Lbs and the DVS150 shall not weigh no more than 617Lbs, includes output cables.

Name: 2.5.04 Factory Environment
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall operate with standard characteristics when operated in a typical factory environment.  The target environment typically has contamination from welding processes, metal foundry processes, and fabrication activities and may include conductive fibers or dust accumulation.  Service and maintenance procedures to maintain standard characteristics are acceptable.

Name: 2.3.10 Efficiency
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall have an efficiency of greater than or equal to 92% at nominal line voltage.  This shall be measured with output power and voltage at greater than 50 % of rated values.

Name: 2.3.11 THD
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall have an input current THD rating of less than 15% at nominal line voltage and full output power conditions.

Name: 2.3.12 Operating Frequency – North America
Author: skellys
Note: The charger nominal operating frequency shall be 60Hz.

Name: 2.3.13 Operating Frequency - International
Author: skellys
Note: The charger nominal operating frequency shall be 50/60Hz.

Name: 2.3.14 Idle Power
Author: skellys
Note: The DVS100 and DVS150 shall not draw more than forty-five (45) Watts of utility power during idle state. This condition shall be satisfied without accessories connected.

Name: 2.4.1 Output Channels
Author: skellys
Note: The DVS100 and DVS150 shall have two output charging ports.

Name: 2.4.2 Voltage Operating Range
Author: skellys
Note:
The DVS100 shall be capable of operating at output voltages from 16V to 120 VDC at either the maximum rated current or the maximum rated output power to support 24, 36, 48, 72 and 80 volt battery packs.

The DVS150 shall be capable of operating at output voltages from 16V to 130 VDC at either the maximum rated current or the maximum rated output power to support 24, 36, 48, 72,  80 and 96 volt battery packs.

Name: 2.4.4 Output Over-Voltage Withstand
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall be capable of withstanding the connection of a 150VDC battery to the output connection without being damaged.  The charger shall not attempt a charge and shall be capable of normal operation once a battery of the appropriate voltage is connected.

Name: 2.3.03 Input Connection Location – North America
Author: skellys
Note: The standard DVS100 and DVS150 input cable location shall be on the center of the charger as viewed from the front. No input cable or strain relief will be supplied with the charger.

Name: 2.3.04 Input Connection Location – International
Author: skellys
Note:
The charger shall be supplied with 4-Conductor wire UL/CSA listed in place and ten feet (3 Meters) of cable measured from the back panel of the charger to the end of the wire.
DVS 100 -
The charger shall be supplied with 4-Conductor 8 AWG wire in place and ten feet (3 Meters) of cable measured from the back panel of the charger to the end of the cable.
DVS 150 -
The charger shall be supplied with 4-Conductor 6 AWG wire in place and ten feet (3 Meters) of cable measured from the back panel of the charger to the end of the cable.

Name: 2.3.05 Input Monitoring
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall have all necessary monitoring to determine when the line voltage conditions could cause damage to the power conversion circuitry. When a condition is detected that could cause damage, the power supply shall not operate and indicate this condition through the fault line or lines.

Name: 2.3.06 Maximum Breaker Rating  - North America
Author: skellys
Note: To minimize the installation cost of the products, the design goal shall be to meet the following maximum input current requirements at nominal line voltage.

Name: 2.3.07 Maximum Breaker Rating - International
Author: skellys
Note: To minimize the installation cost of the products, the design goal shall be to meet the following maximum input current requirements at nominal line voltage.

Name: 2.3.08 Full Load Amperage
Author: skellys
Note: The DVS100 and DVS150 shall be designed to optimize the current draw at peak output power to ensure the smallest standard utility disconnect can be used. Engineering will measure and report max full power and utility draw.

Name: 2.3.09 Power Factor
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall have a power factor of greater than .95 at nominal line voltage and full output power conditions.

Name: 2.2.3 Interface Isolation
Author: skellys
Note: The PosiCharge customer interfaces shall be isolated from high voltage referenced circuitry. Isolation shall be implemented in the serial interfaces to customers and between AC line voltage, ground, and output voltage.  Schematics, component ratings and hi-potential testing shall be used to validate compliance.

Name: 2.2.4 Idle shutdown for CEC- Option
Author: skellys
Note: When this option is installed the control power shall shut off within 30 minutes when no vehicle is connected.  The charger controls shall be powered for 10 minute +- 3 minutes after three-phase AC power is applied.  Idle power shall be less than 10W per CEC requirements.

Name: 2.2.5 Accessory Driver Kit
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall have two (2) Accessory Driver Kit interfaces installed with the required terminal block, wiring harness, and knockout used for installing stack lights, water and ventilation accessories.

Name: 2.2.6 Optional RS-422 Interface
Author: skellys
Note: The charger shall have as an optional item, at the time of purchase, the RS-422 Interface kit. The kit shall also be available to customers to be purchased and installed by field service personnel. This kit shall not ship as part of the baseline configuration.

Name: 2.2.1 Control Panel Interface
Author: skellys
Note:
The charger shall have two (2) Control Panels and each Control Panel shall have a control interface between the front panel control board and the regulation electronics in the charger consisting of the following control signals: Analog Current Command
  • Signal Level = 0-10V
  • DVS 100 = 0-200ADC
  • DVS 150 = 0-300ADC
Digital Enable Line
  • Signal Level = 0/5V
  • DVS 100 = Off/On
  • DVS 150 = Off/On
Analog Current Feedback
  • Signal Level = 0-10V
  • DVS 100 = 0-200ADC
  • DVS 150 = 0-300ADC
Digital Status Line
  • Signal Level = 0/5V
  • DVS 100 = Normal/Fault
  • DVS 150 = Normal/Fault
*Existing Bassi fault/status indicator lights shall be retained.

Name: 2.2.2 Serial Interfaces
Author: skellys
Note:
The charger shall have the following interfaces in the final configuration:
  • BMID – Battery Monitoring and Identification
  • RS232 – Already isolated and available at front panel
  • RS422 – Requires isolation and chassis-mounted output port for use with an external RS-422 Interface device
Note: These interfaces are already a part of the PosiCharge control board but not all are isolated, as BMID does not require isolation. This specification shall be used to verify that the wiring to these interfaces is implemented in the final configuration and isolation is used where identified.

Name: IEC 62752 9.5.5.3.0-6
Author: legaspic
Note:
The series of tests is carried out on an IC-CPD placed on a metal support, wired as in normal
use and being in the closed position.
All components bridging the basic insulation have to be disconnected.
A first series of tests is made, the impulses being applied between:
– the phase pole(s) and the neutral pole connected together, and
– the metal support connected to the terminal(s) intended for the protective conductor(s), if
any.
A second series of tests is made, the impulses being applied between:
– the phase pole(s), connected together, and
– the neutral pole of the IC-CPD.
There shall be no disruptive discharge. If, however, only one such disruptive discharge
occurs, ten additional impulses having the same polarity as that which caused the disruptive
discharge are applied, the connections being the same as those with which the failure
occurred.
No further disruptive discharge shall occur.
Afterwards a new sample is tested according to 9.5.5.3.4.

Name: IEC 62752 9.5.5.3.0-8
Author: legaspic
Note:
Verification shall be performed to ensure that components, bridging the basic insulation and
having been disconnected during the impulse voltage test for testing the basic insulation,
shall not impair the behaviour or the safety of the basic insulation of the equipment during
normal use.
A new IC-CPD sample is tested in order to check that components bridging the basic
insulation would not reduce safety with respect to short term temporary overvoltages.
The test voltage has a frequency of 50/60 Hz. In accordance to IEC 60364-4-44:2007, Table
44.A2 and IEC 60664-1, the r.m.s. value of the test voltage for the basic insulation is 1 200 V
+ Ue. Ue is the nominal voltage value between line and neutral.
NOTE 1 As an example, for an IC-CPD having a rated voltage of Ue = 250 V, the value of the a.c. test voltage for
basic insulation is 1 200 V + 250 V, thus the r.m.s. test voltage is 1 450 V.
The voltage is applied for 5 s between:
– the phase pole(s) and the neutral pole connected together, and
– the metal support connected to the terminal(s) intended for the protective conductor(s), if
any.
The equipment is then visually inspected; no component bridging the basic insulation shall
show a visible alteration.
NOTE 2 It is accepted to replace a fuse before connecting the equipment to the mains. If a fuse protecting a
surge arrester has blown, it is accepted to replace the surge arrester too.
Then, the equipment is connected to the mains in accordance with the manufacturer’s
instruction. Under the condition of 9.7.3.4 the IC-CPD shall trip with a test current of 1,25 I?n.
One test only is made on one pole, taken at random, without measurement of break time.

Name: IEC 62752 9.8.2.1.0-1
Author: legaspic
Note:
The IC-CPD is prepared according to 9.2. The test is made in a test circuit as shown in
Figure 31.
Endurance tests are made at the rate of four operating cycles per minute, if the conditioning of the IC-CPD does not allow this, the test shall be made at the shortest possible time, given by the manufacturer. Switching of S2 shall not be synchronized with the phase angle of the supply. The ON period shall have a duration of 1,9 s to 2,1 s.
IC-CPDs are subjected to a total number of 10 000 operating cycles, each operating cycle
consisting of a closing operation followed by an opening operation.
The test is made at rated operational voltage.
Calibration of the test circuit:
a) the current is recorded through the current sensor A;
b) when supplied at the test voltage the following adjustments are made;
1) calibration of inrush current (R3 and C1): The IC-CPD is replaced by a link BC having
negligible impedance compared with that of the test circuit. S3 and S4 are in open
position. R3 and C1 are adjusted so that after closing S1 at a phase angle of 90° the
current through the current sensor reaches a peak value of 200 A ± 10 A with a rise
time tr (10 % to 90 % of the peak value) of maximum 20µs and declines to a value of
66 A ± 3 A at 30 µs + 20µs after the peak;
2) calibration of rated current (X1): With BC removed, S1, S2 and S3 in closed position
and S4 in open position, X1 is adjusted so that the current through the current sensor
equals the rated current. X1 consists of resistors and reactors in series (X1). If air-core
reactors are used, a resistor taking approximately 0,6 % of the current through the
reactors is connected in parallel with each reactor. If iron-core reactors are used, the
iron-power losses of these reactors shall not appreciably influence the recovery
voltage. The current shall have substantially sine-wave form and the power factor shall
be at least 0,95;
3) calibration of pre-charge current (R2) if the rated current of the device is lower than
30 A: With the IC-CPD replaced by link BC, having negligible impedance compared
with that of the test circuit and S1, S2, S3 and S4 in closed position, R2 is adjusted so
that the current through the current sensor equals 30 A r.m.s. If the rated current of the
device is higher than 30 A, R2 is replaced by an open circuit.
The inrush current consists of two superimposed components, both starting at the same time
at the closing of the contactors in the IC-CPD:
– The resulting test current has a peak of maximum 230 A and corresponds to the Event 1 of
ISO 17409:–, 8.8.2.
– This peak value decay to 30 A r.m,s. This (sinusoidal) current remains up to 1 s and
corresponds to the Event 2 of ISO 17409:–, 8.8.2.
A principal wave shape is shown in Figure 33.

Note:

Five test cycles are performed (see Figure 27).
Within 6 h the ambient air temperature is reduced to -25 °C ± 2 °C without any supply of
humidity and is kept at this value for 6 h. Within the next 6 h the temperature is increased to
+23 °C ± 2 °C and the relative humidity is increased to 93 % ± 3 %.
These values are again kept for 6 h (end of first cycle).
This cycle is performed five times. During these cycles the IC-CPD shall not trip.
Prior to the end of the last 6 h period at -25 °C a residual current is passed through one pole
of the IC-CPD.
The IC-CPD shall trip within 0,3 s
– at an alternating residual current of 1,25 I?n, and
– at a pulsating residual current (one-way rectification, a = 0°el) of 1,25 × 1,4 I?n for
IC-CPDs with I?n > 6 mA and by a factor 2 for IC-CPDs with I?n = 6 mA.

Name: IEC 62752 9.5.5.2.0-1
Author: legaspic
Note:
If the measurement of the clearances of items 2 and 4 in Table 7 and the arrangements given
in 9.5.2 b), c) d) and e) shows a reduction of the required length this test applies. This test is
carried out immediately after the measurement of the insulation resistance in 9.5.3.
NOTE The measurement of the clearances can be replaced by this test.
The test is carried out on an IC-CPD placed on a metal support and being in the closed
position.
The test impulse voltage values shall be as given in Table 10. These values are corrected for
the altitude at which the tests are carried out, according to Table 10.
A first series of tests is made applying the impulse voltage between:
– the phase pole(s) and the neutral pole connected together, and
– the metal support connected to the terminal(s) intended for the protective conductor(s), if
any.
A second series of tests is made applying the impulse voltage between:
– the phase pole(s), connected together, and
– the neutral pole of the IC-CPD, as applicable.
A third series of tests is made applying the impulse voltage between the arrangements given
in 9.5.2 b), c), d) and e) and not tested during the two first sequences described here above.
A fourth series of tests for verification of double insulation or reinforced insulation is made
applying the impulse voltage between hazardous-live parts and

material), and

There shall be no disruptive discharge. If, however, only one such disruptive discharge
